# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1410
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1410
- **Title**: fix(1408): harness-induced bench failures — isolated job logs, redacted at rest, shape-only bash interceptor (AC1–AC3; AC4 documented)
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/1408-bench-harness-artifacts` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 22
- **Additions**: +730
- **Deletions**: -16
- **Created**: 2026-10-08T11:25:01Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-08T12:07:09Z

## PR Description

Fixes #1408 (harness ACs). Bench-autopsy r3, run 37736364517: **~half of the non-stall failures were harness-induced, not agent failures.** This PR fixes the harness side (AC1–AC3) and root-causes AC4 with no code change, as the AC directs.

## AC1 — bench/unattended artifacts leave the task workspace
Evidence (H1, CONFIRMED ×2): `sanitize-git-repo`/`.hard` passed both secret tests and failed ONLY `test_no_other_files_changed` — fa's bash-job logs at `<task-cwd>/.fah/bash_jobs/` captured raw secrets from the agent's own greps; the agent sanitized its own harness logs; the extra modified files flipped the graded diff. The session root was already outside (`--session-root /agent-logs|/logs/agent/fah-sessions`); job logs were not.

- `ShellJobRegistry.jobLogDir` (default unchanged: `<cwd>/.fah/bash_jobs`), resolved at boot from `FAH_JOB_LOG_DIR` (`jobLogDirOverride`; lib/ stays dart:io-free, the executable passes `Platform.environment`).
- The terminal-bench and harbor adapters export `FAH_JOB_LOG_DIR=/tmp/fa-harness-artifacts/bash_jobs` — the in-container twin of $RUNNER_TEMP (pinned by a python UT on both adapters' env).
- UT: a run with the override leaves **no `.fah/` in the task dir** after completion; default location pinned for compat.

## AC2 — job logs redacted at rest
Evidence (H1): the logs are documented as NOT redacted and leaked real dataset secrets onto shared runners. Every detached job's log writes now pass through a line-buffered `JobLogRedactor` (new, `lib/src/env/`) **before** the size ceiling, so the resting file carries `[REDACTED:<kind>]` markers; a secret split across stream chunks still masks and the settle path flushes the trailing partial line. The CLI wires the same `RedactionPipeline` that masks tool results into the registry; the option forwards through every options rewrap (secrets/session-vars/cwd decorators, cube sandbox). The live output stream stays raw (transient; feeds the password detector) — at-rest is the contract, and `bash_job output` tails the redacted file.

- UTs: registry-level and LocalShell-level — a job echoing a fixture AWS access key leaves the marker on disk, never the secret; registered non-vendor secrets mask; no-redactor hosts keep byte-identical logs.

## AC3 — the interceptor never rewrites agent-authored identifiers
Evidence (H2, CONFIRMED): `configure-git-webserver` — the transcript records *"The literal key filename got mangled by a filter — I'll use a different key name."* A filter rewrote text inside a FILENAME the agent was creating; the agent found out via I/O errors.

- New `redactBashCommandSecretShapes` (`lib/src/approval/bash_shape_redaction.dart`): **only a recognized secret SHAPE** — a vendor token regex match (AWS `AKIA+16`, GitHub `ghp_`, OpenAI `sk-`, JWT, …) — is ever rewritten to `[REDACTED:<kind>]`. Key-like-but-unmatched text (random filenames, entropy-heavy identifiers, hex runs) stays byte-identical: no heuristic ever mutates agent-authored command text.
- The bash tool executes the rewritten command and prefixes the tool result with a notice **naming exactly what changed** (count + every shape label) on all three paths (foreground, yield-job, background) — the agent sees the rewrite instead of discovering corruption by failure.
- UTs: (a) a command creating a file whose name contains a key-like token is NOT rewritten (and runs byte-identically, no notice); (b) a true secret shape IS rewritten and the notice names it.

## AC4 — H4 root cause: no propagation bug; prompt-contract candidate (no code, per the AC)
Traced the full env path for the `create-bucket` trial: `LocalShell._environment` = `{...Platform.environment, ...?given}` — ambient env is inherited, `ShellExecOptions.env` overrides, never replaces (`lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart`; pinned by the existing UT `env overrides merge over the host environment` in `test/env/io_execution_env_test.dart`). Every decorator (secrets, session-vars, cwd) merges additively; the bash tool passes no env; the adapters launch fa via docker-exec/tmux inside the task container, so compose-level task env reaches fa's process and its bash children. There is no env filtering/allowlist anywhere in the exec path. Conclusion: the creds the agent failed to find were **genuinely absent from that trial's container** (agent checked `aws configure list` + env, asked via request_secret, was declined unattended, stopped cleanly) — a task-side provisioning gap, not an fa bug. Documented as a **prompt-contract candidate**: "hunt credentials in common places (~/.aws/, /run/secrets/*, task files, metadata endpoints, localstack endpoint env) before declaring them missing", pairing with #1407's repeat-unresolved audit (H3's crashing test belongs there too).

## Tests
TDD; test files mirror lib/ structure (`test/approval/bash_shape_redaction_test.dart`, `test/tools/shell_jobs_isolation_test.dart`, groups in `test/env/shell_job_io_test.dart`, `HarnessArtifactIsolationTest` in `bench/terminal_bench/test_fa_agent_timeout.py`). New code stays well under the 2800-line ceiling (largest touched file 1333 lines) and every new method is small (CC ≤ 8) and covered. Python suite: 234 tests, 1 pre-existing env failure unrelated to this branch (`test_sitecustomize` needs py≥3.10 `assertNoLogs`). Dart VM is unavailable in this lane (SIGKILLed) — changes verified by close reading; the gate re-runs in CI.

Fixes #1408

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1410
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1410
- **Title**: fix(1408): harness-induced bench failures — isolated job logs, redacted at rest, shape-only bash interceptor (AC1–AC3; AC4 documented)
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/1408-bench-harness-artifacts` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 22
- **Additions**: +730
- **Deletions**: -16
- **Created**: 2026-10-08T11:25:01Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-08T12:07:09Z

## PR Description

Fixes #1408 (harness ACs). Bench-autopsy r3, run 37736364517: **~half of the non-stall failures were harness-induced, not agent failures.** This PR fixes the harness side (AC1–AC3) and root-causes AC4 with no code change, as the AC directs.

## AC1 — bench/unattended artifacts leave the task workspace
Evidence (H1, CONFIRMED ×2): `sanitize-git-repo`/`.hard` passed both secret tests and failed ONLY `test_no_other_files_changed` — fa's bash-job logs at `<task-cwd>/.fah/bash_jobs/` captured raw secrets from the agent's own greps; the agent sanitized its own harness logs; the extra modified files flipped the graded diff. The session root was already outside (`--session-root /agent-logs|/logs/agent/fah-sessions`); job logs were not.

- `ShellJobRegistry.jobLogDir` (default unchanged: `<cwd>/.fah/bash_jobs`), resolved at boot from `FAH_JOB_LOG_DIR` (`jobLogDirOverride`; lib/ stays dart:io-free, the executable passes `Platform.environment`).
- The terminal-bench and harbor adapters export `FAH_JOB_LOG_DIR=/tmp/fa-harness-artifacts/bash_jobs` — the in-container twin of $RUNNER_TEMP (pinned by a python UT on both adapters' env).
- UT: a run with the override leaves **no `.fah/` in the task dir** after completion; default location pinned for compat.

## AC2 — job logs redacted at rest
Evidence (H1): the logs are documented as NOT redacted and leaked real dataset secrets onto shared runners. Every detached job's log writes now pass through a line-buffered `JobLogRedactor` (new, `lib/src/env/`) **before** the size ceiling, so the resting file carries `[REDACTED:<kind>]` markers; a secret split across stream chunks still masks and the settle path flushes the trailing partial line. The CLI wires the same `RedactionPipeline` that masks tool results into the registry; the option forwards through every options rewrap (secrets/session-vars/cwd decorators, cube sandbox). The live output stream stays raw (transient; feeds the password detector) — at-rest is the contract, and `bash_job output` tails the redacted file.

- UTs: registry-level and LocalShell-level — a job echoing a fixture AWS access key leaves the marker on disk, never the secret; registered non-vendor secrets mask; no-redactor hosts keep byte-identical logs.

## AC3 — the interceptor never rewrites agent-authored identifiers
Evidence (H2, CONFIRMED): `configure-git-webserver` — the transcript records *"The literal key filename got mangled by a filter — I'll use a different key name."* A filter rewrote text inside a FILENAME the agent was creating; the agent found out via I/O errors.

- New `redactBashCommandSecretShapes` (`lib/src/approval/bash_shape_redaction.dart`): **only a recognized secret SHAPE** — a vendor token regex match (AWS `AKIA+16`, GitHub `ghp_`, OpenAI `sk-`, JWT, …) — is ever rewritten to `[REDACTED:<kind>]`. Key-like-but-unmatched text (random filenames, entropy-heavy identifiers, hex runs) stays byte-identical: no heuristic ever mutates agent-authored command text.
- The bash tool executes the rewritten command and prefixes the tool result with a notice **naming exactly what changed** (count + every shape label) on all three paths (foreground, yield-job, background) — the agent sees the rewrite instead of discovering corruption by failure.
- UTs: (a) a command creating a file whose name contains a key-like token is NOT rewritten (and runs byte-identically, no notice); (b) a true secret shape IS rewritten and the notice names it.

## AC4 — H4 root cause: no propagation bug; prompt-contract candidate (no code, per the AC)
Traced the full env path for the `create-bucket` trial: `LocalShell._environment` = `{...Platform.environment, ...?given}` — ambient env is inherited, `ShellExecOptions.env` overrides, never replaces (`lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart`; pinned by the existing UT `env overrides merge over the host environment` in `test/env/io_execution_env_test.dart`). Every decorator (secrets, session-vars, cwd) merges additively; the bash tool passes no env; the adapters launch fa via docker-exec/tmux inside the task container, so compose-level task env reaches fa's process and its bash children. There is no env filtering/allowlist anywhere in the exec path. Conclusion: the creds the agent failed to find were **genuinely absent from that trial's container** (agent checked `aws configure list` + env, asked via request_secret, was declined unattended, stopped cleanly) — a task-side provisioning gap, not an fa bug. Documented as a **prompt-contract candidate**: "hunt credentials in common places (~/.aws/, /run/secrets/*, task files, metadata endpoints, localstack endpoint env) before declaring them missing", pairing with #1407's repeat-unresolved audit (H3's crashing test belongs there too).

## Tests
TDD; test files mirror lib/ structure (`test/approval/bash_shape_redaction_test.dart`, `test/tools/shell_jobs_isolation_test.dart`, groups in `test/env/shell_job_io_test.dart`, `HarnessArtifactIsolationTest` in `bench/terminal_bench/test_fa_agent_timeout.py`). New code stays well under the 2800-line ceiling (largest touched file 1333 lines) and every new method is small (CC ≤ 8) and covered. Python suite: 234 tests, 1 pre-existing env failure unrelated to this branch (`test_sitecustomize` needs py≥3.10 `assertNoLogs`). Dart VM is unavailable in this lane (SIGKILLed) — changes verified by close reading; the gate re-runs in CI.

Fixes #1408

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1410
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1410
- **Title**: fix(1408): harness-induced bench failures — isolated job logs, redacted at rest, shape-only bash interceptor (AC1–AC3; AC4 documented)
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/1408-bench-harness-artifacts` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 22
- **Additions**: +730
- **Deletions**: -16
- **Created**: 2026-10-08T11:25:01Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-08T12:07:09Z

## PR Description

Fixes #1408 (harness ACs). Bench-autopsy r3, run 37736364517: **~half of the non-stall failures were harness-induced, not agent failures.** This PR fixes the harness side (AC1–AC3) and root-causes AC4 with no code change, as the AC directs.

## AC1 — bench/unattended artifacts leave the task workspace
Evidence (H1, CONFIRMED ×2): `sanitize-git-repo`/`.hard` passed both secret tests and failed ONLY `test_no_other_files_changed` — fa's bash-job logs at `<task-cwd>/.fah/bash_jobs/` captured raw secrets from the agent's own greps; the agent sanitized its own harness logs; the extra modified files flipped the graded diff. The session root was already outside (`--session-root /agent-logs|/logs/agent/fah-sessions`); job logs were not.

- `ShellJobRegistry.jobLogDir` (default unchanged: `<cwd>/.fah/bash_jobs`), resolved at boot from `FAH_JOB_LOG_DIR` (`jobLogDirOverride`; lib/ stays dart:io-free, the executable passes `Platform.environment`).
- The terminal-bench and harbor adapters export `FAH_JOB_LOG_DIR=/tmp/fa-harness-artifacts/bash_jobs` — the in-container twin of $RUNNER_TEMP (pinned by a python UT on both adapters' env).
- UT: a run with the override leaves **no `.fah/` in the task dir** after completion; default location pinned for compat.

## AC2 — job logs redacted at rest
Evidence (H1): the logs are documented as NOT redacted and leaked real dataset secrets onto shared runners. Every detached job's log writes now pass through a line-buffered `JobLogRedactor` (new, `lib/src/env/`) **before** the size ceiling, so the resting file carries `[REDACTED:<kind>]` markers; a secret split across stream chunks still masks and the settle path flushes the trailing partial line. The CLI wires the same `RedactionPipeline` that masks tool results into the registry; the option forwards through every options rewrap (secrets/session-vars/cwd decorators, cube sandbox). The live output stream stays raw (transient; feeds the password detector) — at-rest is the contract, and `bash_job output` tails the redacted file.

- UTs: registry-level and LocalShell-level — a job echoing a fixture AWS access key leaves the marker on disk, never the secret; registered non-vendor secrets mask; no-redactor hosts keep byte-identical logs.

## AC3 — the interceptor never rewrites agent-authored identifiers
Evidence (H2, CONFIRMED): `configure-git-webserver` — the transcript records *"The literal key filename got mangled by a filter — I'll use a different key name."* A filter rewrote text inside a FILENAME the agent was creating; the agent found out via I/O errors.

- New `redactBashCommandSecretShapes` (`lib/src/approval/bash_shape_redaction.dart`): **only a recognized secret SHAPE** — a vendor token regex match (AWS `AKIA+16`, GitHub `ghp_`, OpenAI `sk-`, JWT, …) — is ever rewritten to `[REDACTED:<kind>]`. Key-like-but-unmatched text (random filenames, entropy-heavy identifiers, hex runs) stays byte-identical: no heuristic ever mutates agent-authored command text.
- The bash tool executes the rewritten command and prefixes the tool result with a notice **naming exactly what changed** (count + every shape label) on all three paths (foreground, yield-job, background) — the agent sees the rewrite instead of discovering corruption by failure.
- UTs: (a) a command creating a file whose name contains a key-like token is NOT rewritten (and runs byte-identically, no notice); (b) a true secret shape IS rewritten and the notice names it.

## AC4 — H4 root cause: no propagation bug; prompt-contract candidate (no code, per the AC)
Traced the full env path for the `create-bucket` trial: `LocalShell._environment` = `{...Platform.environment, ...?given}` — ambient env is inherited, `ShellExecOptions.env` overrides, never replaces (`lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart`; pinned by the existing UT `env overrides merge over the host environment` in `test/env/io_execution_env_test.dart`). Every decorator (secrets, session-vars, cwd) merges additively; the bash tool passes no env; the adapters launch fa via docker-exec/tmux inside the task container, so compose-level task env reaches fa's process and its bash children. There is no env filtering/allowlist anywhere in the exec path. Conclusion: the creds the agent failed to find were **genuinely absent from that trial's container** (agent checked `aws configure list` + env, asked via request_secret, was declined unattended, stopped cleanly) — a task-side provisioning gap, not an fa bug. Documented as a **prompt-contract candidate**: "hunt credentials in common places (~/.aws/, /run/secrets/*, task files, metadata endpoints, localstack endpoint env) before declaring them missing", pairing with #1407's repeat-unresolved audit (H3's crashing test belongs there too).

## Tests
TDD; test files mirror lib/ structure (`test/approval/bash_shape_redaction_test.dart`, `test/tools/shell_jobs_isolation_test.dart`, groups in `test/env/shell_job_io_test.dart`, `HarnessArtifactIsolationTest` in `bench/terminal_bench/test_fa_agent_timeout.py`). New code stays well under the 2800-line ceiling (largest touched file 1333 lines) and every new method is small (CC ≤ 8) and covered. Python suite: 234 tests, 1 pre-existing env failure unrelated to this branch (`test_sitecustomize` needs py≥3.10 `assertNoLogs`). Dart VM is unavailable in this lane (SIGKILLed) — changes verified by close reading; the gate re-runs in CI.

Fixes #1408

Every detached job's log writes now pass through a line-buffered `JobLogRedactor` (new, `lib/src/env/`) **before** the size ceiling, so the resting file carries `[REDACTED:<kind>]` markers; a secret split across stream chunks still masks and the settle path flushes the trailing partial line. The CLI wires the same `RedactionPipeline` that masks tool results into the registry; the option forwards through every options rewrap (secrets/session-vars/cwd decorators, cube sandbox). The live output stream stays raw (transient; feeds the password detector) — at-rest is the contract, and `bash_job output` tails the redacted file.

- UTs: registry-level and LocalShell-level — a job echoing a fixture AWS access key leaves the marker on disk, never the secret; registered non-vendor secrets mask; no-redactor hosts keep byte-identical logs.

## AC3 — the interceptor never rewrites agent-authored identifiers
Evidence (H2, CONFIRMED): `configure-git-webserver` — the transcript records *"The literal key filename got mangled by a filter — I'll use a different key name."* A filter rewrote text inside a FILENAME the agent was creating; the agent found out via I/O errors.

- New `redactBashCommandSecretShapes` (`lib/src/approval/bash_shape_redaction.dart`): **only a recognized secret SHAPE** — a vendor token regex match (AWS `AKIA+16`, GitHub `ghp_`, OpenAI `sk-`, JWT, …) — is ever rewritten to `[REDACTED:<kind>]`. Key-like-but-unmatched text (random filenames, entropy-heavy identifiers, hex runs) stays byte-identical: no heuristic ever mutates agent-authored command text.
- The bash tool executes the rewritten command and prefixes the tool result with a notice **naming exactly what changed** (count + every shape label) on all three paths (foreground, yield-job, background) — the agent sees the rewrite instead of discovering corruption by failure.
- UTs: (a) a command creating a file whose name contains a key-like token is NOT rewritten (and runs byte-identically, no notice); (b) a true secret shape IS rewritten and the notice names it.

## AC4 — H4 root cause: no propagation bug; prompt-contract candidate (no code, per the AC)
Traced the full env path for the `create-bucket` trial: `LocalShell._environment` = `{...Platform.environment, ...?given}` — ambient env is inherited, `ShellExecOptions.env` overrides, never replaces (`lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart`; pinned by the existing UT `env overrides merge over the host environment` in `test/env/io_execution_env_test.dart`). Every decorator (secrets, session-vars, cwd) merges additively; the bash tool passes no env; the adapters launch fa via docker-exec/tmux inside the task container, so compose-level task env reaches fa's process and its bash children. There is no env filtering/allowlist anywhere in the exec path. Conclusion: the creds the agent failed to find were **genuinely absent from that trial's container** (agent checked `aws configure list` + env, asked via request_secret, was declined unattended, stopped cleanly) — a task-side provisioning gap, not an fa bug. Documented as a **prompt-contract candidate**: "hunt credentials in common places (~/.aws/, /run/secrets/*, task files, metadata endpoints, localstack endpoint env) before declaring them missing", pairing with #1407's repeat-unresolved audit (H3's crashing test belongs there too).

## Tests
TDD; test files mirror lib/ structure (`test/approval/bash_shape_redaction_test.dart`, `test/tools/shell_jobs_isolation_test.dart`, groups in `test/env/shell_job_io_test.dart`, `HarnessArtifactIsolationTest` in `bench/terminal_bench/test_fa_agent_timeout.py`). New code stays well under the 2800-line ceiling (largest touched file 1333 lines) and every new method is small (CC ≤ 8) and covered. Python suite: 234 tests, 1 pre-existing env failure unrelated to this branch (`test_sitecustomize` needs py≥3.10 `assertNoLogs`). Dart VM is unavailable in this lane (SIGKILLed) — changes verified by close reading; the gate re-runs in CI.

All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. Findings on unchanged code outside the diff belong in `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, not as inline comments. Do NOT write `outputs/response.md`; the review is posted to GitHub only. ```mermaid flowchart TD O1["Write outputs/pr_review.json — structured data for GitHub PR review…

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1410
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1410
- **Title**: fix(1408): harness-induced bench failures — isolated job logs, redacted at rest, shape-only bash interceptor (AC1–AC3; AC4 documented)
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/1408-bench-harness-artifacts` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 22
- **Additions**: +730
- **Deletions**: -16
- **Created**: 2026-10-08T11:25:01Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-08T12:07:09Z

## PR Description

Fixes #1408 (harness ACs). Bench-autopsy r3, run 37736364517: **~half of the non-stall failures were harness-induced, not agent failures.** This PR fixes the harness side (AC1–AC3) and root-causes AC4 with no code change, as the AC directs.

## AC1 — bench/unattended artifacts leave the task workspace
Evidence (H1, CONFIRMED ×2): `sanitize-git-repo`/`.hard` passed both secret tests and failed ONLY `test_no_other_files_changed` — fa's bash-job logs at `<task-cwd>/.fah/bash_jobs/` captured raw secrets from the agent's own greps; the agent sanitized its own harness logs; the extra modified files flipped the graded diff. The session root was already outside (`--session-root /agent-logs|/logs/agent/fah-sessions`); job logs were not.

- `ShellJobRegistry.jobLogDir` (default unchanged: `<cwd>/.fah/bash_jobs`), resolved at boot from `FAH_JOB_LOG_DIR` (`jobLogDirOverride`; lib/ stays dart:io-free, the executable passes `Platform.environment`).
- The terminal-bench and harbor adapters export `FAH_JOB_LOG_DIR=/tmp/fa-harness-artifacts/bash_jobs` — the in-container twin of $RUNNER_TEMP (pinned by a python UT on both adapters' env).
- UT: a run with the override leaves **no `.fah/` in the task dir** after completion; default location pinned for compat.

## AC2 — job logs redacted at rest
Evidence (H1): the logs are documented as NOT redacted and leaked real dataset secrets onto shared runners. Every detached job's log writes now pass through a line-buffered `JobLogRedactor` (new, `lib/src/env/`) **before** the size ceiling, so the resting file carries `[REDACTED:<kind>]` markers; a secret split across stream chunks still masks and the settle path flushes the trailing partial line. The CLI wires the same `RedactionPipeline` that masks tool results into the registry; the option forwards through every options rewrap (secrets/session-vars/cwd decorators, cube sandbox). The live output stream stays raw (transient; feeds the password detector) — at-rest is the contract, and `bash_job output` tails the redacted file.

- UTs: registry-level and LocalShell-level — a job echoing a fixture AWS access key leaves the marker on disk, never the secret; registered non-vendor secrets mask; no-redactor hosts keep byte-identical logs.

## AC3 — the interceptor never rewrites agent-authored identifiers
Evidence (H2, CONFIRMED): `configure-git-webserver` — the transcript records *"The literal key filename got mangled by a filter — I'll use a different key name."* A filter rewrote text inside a FILENAME the agent was creating; the agent found out via I/O errors.

- New `redactBashCommandSecretShapes` (`lib/src/approval/bash_shape_redaction.dart`): **only a recognized secret SHAPE** — a vendor token regex match (AWS `AKIA+16`, GitHub `ghp_`, OpenAI `sk-`, JWT, …) — is ever rewritten to `[REDACTED:<kind>]`. Key-like-but-unmatched text (random filenames, entropy-heavy identifiers, hex runs) stays byte-identical: no heuristic ever mutates agent-authored command text.
- The bash tool executes the rewritten command and prefixes the tool result with a notice **naming exactly what changed** (count + every shape label) on all three paths (foreground, yield-job, background) — the agent sees the rewrite instead of discovering corruption by failure.
- UTs: (a) a command creating a file whose name contains a key-like token is NOT rewritten (and runs byte-identically, no notice); (b) a true secret shape IS rewritten and the notice names it.

## AC4 — H4 root cause: no propagation bug; prompt-contract candidate (no code, per the AC)
Traced the full env path for the `create-bucket` trial: `LocalShell._environment` = `{...Platform.environment, ...?given}` — ambient env is inherited, `ShellExecOptions.env` overrides, never replaces (`lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart`; pinned by the existing UT `env overrides merge over the host environment` in `test/env/io_execution_env_test.dart`). Every decorator (secrets, session-vars, cwd) merges additively; the bash tool passes no env; the adapters launch fa via docker-exec/tmux inside the task container, so compose-level task env reaches fa's process and its bash children. There is no env filtering/allowlist anywhere in the exec path. Conclusion: the creds the agent failed to find were **genuinely absent from that trial's container** (agent checked `aws configure list` + env, asked via request_secret, was declined unattended, stopped cleanly) — a task-side provisioning gap, not an fa bug. Documented as a **prompt-contract candidate**: "hunt credentials in common places (~/.aws/, /run/secrets/*, task files, metadata endpoints, localstack endpoint env) before declaring them missing", pairing with #1407's repeat-unresolved audit (H3's crashing test belongs there too).

## Tests
TDD; test files mirror lib/ structure (`test/approval/bash_shape_redaction_test.dart`, `test/tools/shell_jobs_isolation_test.dart`, groups in `test/env/shell_job_io_test.dart`, `HarnessArtifactIsolationTest` in `bench/terminal_bench/test_fa_agent_timeout.py`). New code stays well under the 2800-line ceiling (largest touched file 1333 lines) and every new method is small (CC ≤ 8) and covered. Python suite: 234 tests, 1 pre-existing env failure unrelated to this branch (`test_sitecustomize` needs py≥3.10 `assertNoLogs`). Dart VM is unavailable in this lane (SIGKILLed) — changes verified by close reading; the gate re-runs in CI.

Fixes #1408

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1410
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1410
- **Title**: fix(1408): harness-induced bench failures — isolated job logs, redacted at rest, shape-only bash interceptor (AC1–AC3; AC4 documented)
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/1408-bench-harness-artifacts` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 22
- **Additions**: +730
- **Deletions**: -16
- **Created**: 2026-10-08T11:25:01Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-08T12:07:09Z

## PR Description

Fixes #1408 (harness ACs). Bench-autopsy r3, run 37736364517: **~half of the non-stall failures were harness-induced, not agent failures.** This PR fixes the harness side (AC1–AC3) and root-causes AC4 with no code change, as the AC directs.

## AC1 — bench/unattended artifacts leave the task workspace
Evidence (H1, CONFIRMED ×2): `sanitize-git-repo`/`.hard` passed both secret tests and failed ONLY `test_no_other_files_changed` — fa's bash-job logs at `<task-cwd>/.fah/bash_jobs/` captured raw secrets from the agent's own greps; the agent sanitized its own harness logs; the extra modified files flipped the graded diff. The session root was already outside (`--session-root /agent-logs|/logs/agent/fah-sessions`); job logs were not.

- `ShellJobRegistry.jobLogDir` (default unchanged: `<cwd>/.fah/bash_jobs`), resolved at boot from `FAH_JOB_LOG_DIR` (`jobLogDirOverride`; lib/ stays dart:io-free, the executable passes `Platform.environment`).
- The terminal-bench and harbor adapters export `FAH_JOB_LOG_DIR=/tmp/fa-harness-artifacts/bash_jobs` — the in-container twin of $RUNNER_TEMP (pinned by a python UT on both adapters' env).
- UT: a run with the override leaves **no `.fah/` in the task dir** after completion; default location pinned for compat.

## AC2 — job logs redacted at rest
Evidence (H1): the logs are documented as NOT redacted and leaked real dataset secrets onto shared runners. Every detached job's log writes now pass through a line-buffered `JobLogRedactor` (new, `lib/src/env/`) **before** the size ceiling, so the resting file carries `[REDACTED:<kind>]` markers; a secret split across stream chunks still masks and the settle path flushes the trailing partial line. The CLI wires the same `RedactionPipeline` that masks tool results into the registry; the option forwards through every options rewrap (secrets/session-vars/cwd decorators, cube sandbox). The live output stream stays raw (transient; feeds the password detector) — at-rest is the contract, and `bash_job output` tails the redacted file.

- UTs: registry-level and LocalShell-level — a job echoing a fixture AWS access key leaves the marker on disk, never the secret; registered non-vendor secrets mask; no-redactor hosts keep byte-identical logs.

## AC3 — the interceptor never rewrites agent-authored identifiers
Evidence (H2, CONFIRMED): `configure-git-webserver` — the transcript records *"The literal key filename got mangled by a filter — I'll use a different key name."* A filter rewrote text inside a FILENAME the agent was creating; the agent found out via I/O errors.

- New `redactBashCommandSecretShapes` (`lib/src/approval/bash_shape_redaction.dart`): **only a recognized secret SHAPE** — a vendor token regex match (AWS `AKIA+16`, GitHub `ghp_`, OpenAI `sk-`, JWT, …) — is ever rewritten to `[REDACTED:<kind>]`. Key-like-but-unmatched text (random filenames, entropy-heavy identifiers, hex runs) stays byte-identical: no heuristic ever mutates agent-authored command text.
- The bash tool executes the rewritten command and prefixes the tool result with a notice **naming exactly what changed** (count + every shape label) on all three paths (foreground, yield-job, background) — the agent sees the rewrite instead of discovering corruption by failure.
- UTs: (a) a command creating a file whose name contains a key-like token is NOT rewritten (and runs byte-identically, no notice); (b) a true secret shape IS rewritten and the notice names it.

## AC4 — H4 root cause: no propagation bug; prompt-contract candidate (no code, per the AC)
Traced the full env path for the `create-bucket` trial: `LocalShell._environment` = `{...Platform.environment, ...?given}` — ambient env is inherited, `ShellExecOptions.env` overrides, never replaces (`lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart`; pinned by the existing UT `env overrides merge over the host environment` in `test/env/io_execution_env_test.dart`). Every decorator (secrets, session-vars, cwd) merges additively; the bash tool passes no env; the adapters launch fa via docker-exec/tmux inside the task container, so compose-level task env reaches fa's process and its bash children. There is no env filtering/allowlist anywhere in the exec path. Conclusion: the creds the agent failed to find were **genuinely absent from that trial's container** (agent checked `aws configure list` + env, asked via request_secret, was declined unattended, stopped cleanly) — a task-side provisioning gap, not an fa bug. Documented as a **prompt-contract candidate**: "hunt credentials in common places (~/.aws/, /run/secrets/*, task files, metadata endpoints, localstack endpoint env) before declaring them missing", pairing with #1407's repeat-unresolved audit (H3's crashing test belongs there too).

## Tests
TDD; test files mirror lib/ structure (`test/approval/bash_shape_redaction_test.dart`, `test/tools/shell_jobs_isolation_test.dart`, groups in `test/env/shell_job_io_test.dart`, `HarnessArtifactIsolationTest` in `bench/terminal_bench/test_fa_agent_timeout.py`). New code stays well under the 2800-line ceiling (largest touched file 1333 lines) and every new method is small (CC ≤ 8) and covered. Python suite: 234 tests, 1 pre-existing env failure unrelated to this branch (`test_sitecustomize` needs py≥3.10 `assertNoLogs`). Dart VM is unavailable in this lane (SIGKILLed) — changes verified by close reading; the gate re-runs in CI.

Fixes #1408

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1410
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1410
- **Title**: fix(1408): harness-induced bench failures — isolated job logs, redacted at rest, shape-only bash interceptor (AC1–AC3; AC4 documented)
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/1408-bench-harness-artifacts` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 22
- **Additions**: +730
- **Deletions**: -16
- **Created**: 2026-10-08T11:25:01Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-08T12:07:09Z

## PR Description

Fixes #1408 (harness ACs). Bench-autopsy r3, run 37736364517: **~half of the non-stall failures were harness-induced, not agent failures.** This PR fixes the harness side (AC1–AC3) and root-causes AC4 with no code change, as the AC directs.

## AC1 — bench/unattended artifacts leave the task workspace
Evidence (H1, CONFIRMED ×2): `sanitize-git-repo`/`.hard` passed both secret tests and failed ONLY `test_no_other_files_changed` — fa's bash-job logs at `<task-cwd>/.fah/bash_jobs/` captured raw secrets from the agent's own greps; the agent sanitized its own harness logs; the extra modified files flipped the graded diff. The session root was already outside (`--session-root /agent-logs|/logs/agent/fah-sessions`); job logs were not.

- `ShellJobRegistry.jobLogDir` (default unchanged: `<cwd>/.fah/bash_jobs`), resolved at boot from `FAH_JOB_LOG_DIR` (`jobLogDirOverride`; lib/ stays dart:io-free, the executable passes `Platform.environment`).
- The terminal-bench and harbor adapters export `FAH_JOB_LOG_DIR=/tmp/fa-harness-artifacts/bash_jobs` — the in-container twin of $RUNNER_TEMP (pinned by a python UT on both adapters' env).
- UT: a run with the override leaves **no `.fah/` in the task dir** after completion; default location pinned for compat.

## AC2 — job logs redacted at rest
Evidence (H1): the logs are documented as NOT redacted and leaked real dataset secrets onto shared runners. Every detached job's log writes now pass through a line-buffered `JobLogRedactor` (new, `lib/src/env/`) **before** the size ceiling, so the resting file carries `[REDACTED:<kind>]` markers; a secret split across stream chunks still masks and the settle path flushes the trailing partial line. The CLI wires the same `RedactionPipeline` that masks tool results into the registry; the option forwards through every options rewrap (secrets/session-vars/cwd decorators, cube sandbox). The live output stream stays raw (transient; feeds the password detector) — at-rest is the contract, and `bash_job output` tails the redacted file.

- UTs: registry-level and LocalShell-level — a job echoing a fixture AWS access key leaves the marker on disk, never the secret; registered non-vendor secrets mask; no-redactor hosts keep byte-identical logs.

## AC3 — the interceptor never rewrites agent-authored identifiers
Evidence (H2, CONFIRMED): `configure-git-webserver` — the transcript records *"The literal key filename got mangled by a filter — I'll use a different key name."* A filter rewrote text inside a FILENAME the agent was creating; the agent found out via I/O errors.

- New `redactBashCommandSecretShapes` (`lib/src/approval/bash_shape_redaction.dart`): **only a recognized secret SHAPE** — a vendor token regex match (AWS `AKIA+16`, GitHub `ghp_`, OpenAI `sk-`, JWT, …) — is ever rewritten to `[REDACTED:<kind>]`. Key-like-but-unmatched text (random filenames, entropy-heavy identifiers, hex runs) stays byte-identical: no heuristic ever mutates agent-authored command text.
- The bash tool executes the rewritten command and prefixes the tool result with a notice **naming exactly what changed** (count + every shape label) on all three paths (foreground, yield-job, background) — the agent sees the rewrite instead of discovering corruption by failure.
- UTs: (a) a command creating a file whose name contains a key-like token is NOT rewritten (and runs byte-identically, no notice); (b) a true secret shape IS rewritten and the notice names it.

## AC4 — H4 root cause: no propagation bug; prompt-contract candidate (no code, per the AC)
Traced the full env path for the `create-bucket` trial: `LocalShell._environment` = `{...Platform.environment, ...?given}` — ambient env is inherited, `ShellExecOptions.env` overrides, never replaces (`lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart`; pinned by the existing UT `env overrides merge over the host environment` in `test/env/io_execution_env_test.dart`). Every decorator (secrets, session-vars, cwd) merges additively; the bash tool passes no env; the adapters launch fa via docker-exec/tmux inside the task container, so compose-level task env reaches fa's process and its bash children. There is no env filtering/allowlist anywhere in the exec path. Conclusion: the creds the agent failed to find were **genuinely absent from that trial's container** (agent checked `aws configure list` + env, asked via request_secret, was declined unattended, stopped cleanly) — a task-side provisioning gap, not an fa bug. Documented as a **prompt-contract candidate**: "hunt credentials in common places (~/.aws/, /run/secrets/*, task files, metadata endpoints, localstack endpoint env) before declaring them missing", pairing with #1407's repeat-unresolved audit (H3's crashing test belongs there too).

## Tests
TDD; test files mirror lib/ structure (`test/approval/bash_shape_redaction_test.dart`, `test/tools/shell_jobs_isolation_test.dart`, groups in `test/env/shell_job_io_test.dart`, `HarnessArtifactIsolationTest` in `bench/terminal_bench/test_fa_agent_timeout.py`). New code stays well under the 2800-line ceiling (largest touched file 1333 lines) and every new method is small (CC ≤ 8) and covered. Python suite: 234 tests, 1 pre-existing env failure unrelated to this branch (`test_sitecustomize` needs py≥3.10 `assertNoLogs`). Dart VM is unavailable in this lane (SIGKILLed) — changes verified by close reading; the gate re-runs in CI.

Fixes #1408

- name: dart test cube backends (live kernel legs)
        run: dart test test/cube/backends

      # gh-1059 AC4: the real-keychain runner guard — `security`
      # add/find/delete against the runner's login keychain through the
      # bounded-helper machinery (outcome classification incl. stderr
      # tails, env merge, timeout kill). The group is tagged `integration`
      # (real side effects), so the Linux core shards and the pre-commit
      # gate skip it; this macOS leg is where it actually executes. Skips
      # with a named reason when no `security` binary / default keychain.
      - name: dart test secure key store (macOS Keychain live legs)
        run: dart test test/secrets/secure_key_store_test.dart --tags integration

  static:
    name: Static gates
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: changes
    timeout-minutes: 8
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        with:
          sdk: stable

      - name: Pub cache
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: ~/.pub-cache
          key: pub-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: pub-${{ runner.os }}-

      - run: dart pub get

      # Issue #1234: the ≤2800-line file guard MOVED into crap4dart's loc
      # gate (crap4dart.yaml, wc -l parity verified by the maintainer
      # recipe in the issue) — enforced whole-tree by the
      # `crap4dart check --baseline` Quality-gates step below. The shell
      # find-exec guard (gh-1232 AC2) is gone: one enforcement point, no
      # drifted exclusions.

      # Issue #1100: the fa-web-spa.zip packaging guard (base-tag patch +
      # absolute-/app/ grep) must stay functional on every PR — a release
      # run is the wrong place to first discover a broken guard. Fixture
      # self-test: positive path + all red exits, pure bash, no web build.
      - name: Web SPA packaging guard self-test (#1100)
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          d=$(mktemp -d)
          trap 'rm -rf "$d"' EXIT
          mkdir -p "$d/build"
          printf '<html><head>\n<base href="/app/">\n</head></html>\n' > "$d/build/index.html"
          for f in flutter_service_worker.js flutter_bootstrap.js; do echo "// $f" > "$d/build/$f"; done
          echo '{"name":"fa"}' > "$d/build/manifest.json"
          bash scripts/package_web_spa.sh "$d/build" "$d/out.zip" > /dev/null
          unzip -p "$d/out.zip" index.html | grep -F '<base href="./">'
          # AC4 pin: packaging never mutates its input — the Pages deploy's
          # build dir must stay byte-identical.
          grep -F '<base href="/app/">' "$d/build/index.html"
          # Red exit 1: an absolute /app/ sneaking into a touchpoint.
          echo '{"x":"/app/y"}' > "$d/build/manifest.json"
          if bash scripts/package_web_spa.sh "$d/build" "$d/bad.zip" 2>/dev/null; then
            echo "::error::package_web_spa guard passed a build containing /app/ (AC3 #1100)"
            exit 1
          fi
          # Red exit 2: no base tag to patch.
          echo '{"name":"fa"}' > "$d/build/manifest.json"
          echo '<html></html>' > "$d/build/index.html"
          if bash scripts/package_web_spa.sh "$d/build" "$d/bad2.zip" 2>/dev/null; then
            echo "::error::package_web_spa guard passed an unpatchable base tag (AC1 #1100)"
            exit 1
          fi
          # Red exit 3: a missing touchpoint file.
          rm "$d/build/manifest.json"
          if bash scripts/package_web_spa.sh "$d/build" "$d/bad3.zip" 2>/dev/null; then
            echo "::error::package_web_spa guard passed an incomplete build (AC3 #1100)"
            exit 1
          fi
          # fa1.dev parity pin: both web builds must keep the identical
          # release flags AND the same pinned SDK — the bundle's only edit
          # stays the base tag.
          for wf in .github/workflows/pages.yml .github/workflows/ci.yml; do
            grep -q -- '--release' "$wf" || { echo "::error::$wf lost the --release web flag (#1100 parity)"; exit 1; }
            grep -q -- '--base-href /app/' "$wf" || { echo "::error::$wf lost --base-href /app/ (#1100 parity, pages + bundle must share it)"; exit 1; }
            grep -q "flutter-version: '3.47.x'" "$wf" || { echo "::error::$wf unpinned Flutter SDK (#1100 parity, pages + bundle must share it)"; exit 1; }
          done

      # Issue #433 AC1: README CRAP badge must equal the crap4dart.yaml
      # threshold (they drifted to 8.0-vs-12.0 once). Pure python — runs on
      # every PR, including docs-only ones (a README edit is exactly the
      # drift vector).
      - name: CRAP badge/config sync guard
        run: python3 scripts/check_crap_guards.py

      # gh-1199 AC2: the deterministic-gate boundary is self-enforcing —
      # an integration-tagged test that looks live (real provider URL, or
      # a credential-key literal with no mock/loopback in sight) without
      # the `llm` tag fails the gate. Runs on every PR: a PR adding a live
      # test (E1) is exactly the diff this must catch.

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1410
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1410
- **Title**: fix(1408): harness-induced bench failures — isolated job logs, redacted at rest, shape-only bash interceptor (AC1–AC3; AC4 documented)
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/1408-bench-harness-artifacts` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 22
- **Additions**: +730
- **Deletions**: -16
- **Created**: 2026-10-08T11:25:01Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-08T12:07:09Z

## PR Description

Fixes #1408 (harness ACs). Bench-autopsy r3, run 37736364517: **~half of the non-stall failures were harness-induced, not agent failures.** This PR fixes the harness side (AC1–AC3) and root-causes AC4 with no code change, as the AC directs.

## AC1 — bench/unattended artifacts leave the task workspace
Evidence (H1, CONFIRMED ×2): `sanitize-git-repo`/`.hard` passed both secret tests and failed ONLY `test_no_other_files_changed` — fa's bash-job logs at `<task-cwd>/.fah/bash_jobs/` captured raw secrets from the agent's own greps; the agent sanitized its own harness logs; the extra modified files flipped the graded diff. The session root was already outside (`--session-root /agent-logs|/logs/agent/fah-sessions`); job logs were not.

- `ShellJobRegistry.jobLogDir` (default unchanged: `<cwd>/.fah/bash_jobs`), resolved at boot from `FAH_JOB_LOG_DIR` (`jobLogDirOverride`; lib/ stays dart:io-free, the executable passes `Platform.environment`).
- The terminal-bench and harbor adapters export `FAH_JOB_LOG_DIR=/tmp/fa-harness-artifacts/bash_jobs` — the in-container twin of $RUNNER_TEMP (pinned by a python UT on both adapters' env).
- UT: a run with the override leaves **no `.fah/` in the task dir** after completion; default location pinned for compat.

## AC2 — job logs redacted at rest
Evidence (H1): the logs are documented as NOT redacted and leaked real dataset secrets onto shared runners. Every detached job's log writes now pass through a line-buffered `JobLogRedactor` (new, `lib/src/env/`) **before** the size ceiling, so the resting file carries `[REDACTED:<kind>]` markers; a secret split across stream chunks still masks and the settle path flushes the trailing partial line. The CLI wires the same `RedactionPipeline` that masks tool results into the registry; the option forwards through every options rewrap (secrets/session-vars/cwd decorators, cube sandbox). The live output stream stays raw (transient; feeds the password detector) — at-rest is the contract, and `bash_job output` tails the redacted file.

- UTs: registry-level and LocalShell-level — a job echoing a fixture AWS access key leaves the marker on disk, never the secret; registered non-vendor secrets mask; no-redactor hosts keep byte-identical logs.

## AC3 — the interceptor never rewrites agent-authored identifiers
Evidence (H2, CONFIRMED): `configure-git-webserver` — the transcript records *"The literal key filename got mangled by a filter — I'll use a different key name."* A filter rewrote text inside a FILENAME the agent was creating; the agent found out via I/O errors.

- New `redactBashCommandSecretShapes` (`lib/src/approval/bash_shape_redaction.dart`): **only a recognized secret SHAPE** — a vendor token regex match (AWS `AKIA+16`, GitHub `ghp_`, OpenAI `sk-`, JWT, …) — is ever rewritten to `[REDACTED:<kind>]`. Key-like-but-unmatched text (random filenames, entropy-heavy identifiers, hex runs) stays byte-identical: no heuristic ever mutates agent-authored command text.
- The bash tool executes the rewritten command and prefixes the tool result with a notice **naming exactly what changed** (count + every shape label) on all three paths (foreground, yield-job, background) — the agent sees the rewrite instead of discovering corruption by failure.
- UTs: (a) a command creating a file whose name contains a key-like token is NOT rewritten (and runs byte-identically, no notice); (b) a true secret shape IS rewritten and the notice names it.

## AC4 — H4 root cause: no propagation bug; prompt-contract candidate (no code, per the AC)
Traced the full env path for the `create-bucket` trial: `LocalShell._environment` = `{...Platform.environment, ...?given}` — ambient env is inherited, `ShellExecOptions.env` overrides, never replaces (`lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart`; pinned by the existing UT `env overrides merge over the host environment` in `test/env/io_execution_env_test.dart`). Every decorator (secrets, session-vars, cwd) merges additively; the bash tool passes no env; the adapters launch fa via docker-exec/tmux inside the task container, so compose-level task env reaches fa's process and its bash children. There is no env filtering/allowlist anywhere in the exec path. Conclusion: the creds the agent failed to find were **genuinely absent from that trial's container** (agent checked `aws configure list` + env, asked via request_secret, was declined unattended, stopped cleanly) — a task-side provisioning gap, not an fa bug. Documented as a **prompt-contract candidate**: "hunt credentials in common places (~/.aws/, /run/secrets/*, task files, metadata endpoints, localstack endpoint env) before declaring them missing", pairing with #1407's repeat-unresolved audit (H3's crashing test belongs there too).

## Tests
TDD; test files mirror lib/ structure (`test/approval/bash_shape_redaction_test.dart`, `test/tools/shell_jobs_isolation_test.dart`, groups in `test/env/shell_job_io_test.dart`, `HarnessArtifactIsolationTest` in `bench/terminal_bench/test_fa_agent_timeout.py`). New code stays well under the 2800-line ceiling (largest touched file 1333 lines) and every new method is small (CC ≤ 8) and covered. Python suite: 234 tests, 1 pre-existing env failure unrelated to this branch (`test_sitecustomize` needs py≥3.10 `assertNoLogs`). Dart VM is unavailable in this lane (SIGKILLed) — changes verified by close reading; the gate re-runs in CI.

Fixes #1408

- name: dart test cube backends (live kernel legs)
        run: dart test test/cube/backends

      # gh-1059 AC4: the real-keychain runner guard — `security`
      # add/find/delete against the runner's login keychain through the
      # bounded-helper machinery (outcome classification incl. stderr
      # tails, env merge, timeout kill). The group is tagged `integration`
      # (real side effects), so the Linux core shards and the pre-commit
      # gate skip it; this macOS leg is where it actually executes. Skips
      # with a named reason when no `security` binary / default keychain.
      - name: dart test secure key store (macOS Keychain live legs)
        run: dart test test/secrets/secure_key_store_test.dart --tags integration

  static:
    name: Static gates
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: changes
    timeout-minutes: 8
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        with:
          sdk: stable

      - name: Pub cache
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: ~/.pub-cache
          key: pub-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: pub-${{ runner.os }}-

      - run: dart pub get

      # Issue #1234: the ≤2800-line file guard MOVED into crap4dart's loc
      # gate (crap4dart.yaml, wc -l parity verified by the maintainer
      # recipe in the issue) — enforced whole-tree by the
      # `crap4dart check --baseline` Quality-gates step below. The shell
      # find-exec guard (gh-1232 AC2) is gone: one enforcement point, no
      # drifted exclusions.

      # Issue #1100: the fa-web-spa.zip packaging guard (base-tag patch +
      # absolute-/app/ grep) must stay functional on every PR — a release
      # run is the wrong place to first discover a broken guard. Fixture
      # self-test: positive path + all red exits, pure bash, no web build.
      - name: Web SPA packaging guard self-test (#1100)
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          d=$(mktemp -d)
          trap 'rm -rf "$d"' EXIT
          mkdir -p "$d/build"
          printf '<html><head>\n<base href="/app/">\n</head></html>\n' > "$d/build/index.html"
          for f in flutter_service_worker.js flutter_bootstrap.js; do echo "// $f" > "$d/build/$f"; done
          echo '{"name":"fa"}' > "$d/build/manifest.json"
          bash scripts/package_web_spa.sh "$d/build" "$d/out.zip" > /dev/null
          unzip -p "$d/out.zip" index.html | grep -F '<base href="./">'
          # AC4 pin: packaging never mutates its input — the Pages deploy's
          # build dir must stay byte-identical.
          grep -F '<base href="/app/">' "$d/build/index.html"
          # Red exit 1: an absolute /app/ sneaking into a touchpoint.
          echo '{"x":"/app/y"}' > "$d/build/manifest.json"
          if bash scripts/package_web_spa.sh "$d/build" "$d/bad.zip" 2>/dev/null; then
            echo "::error::package_web_spa guard passed a build containing /app/ (AC3 #1100)"
            exit 1
          fi
          # Red exit 2: no base tag to patch.
          echo '{"name":"fa"}' > "$d/build/manifest.json"
          echo '<html></html>' > "$d/build/index.html"
          if bash scripts/package_web_spa.sh "$d/build" "$d/bad2.zip" 2>/dev/null; then
            echo "::error::package_web_spa guard passed an unpatchable base tag (AC1 #1100)"
            exit 1
          fi
          # Red exit 3: a missing touchpoint file.
          rm "$d/build/manifest.json"
          if bash scripts/package_web_spa.sh "$d/build" "$d/bad3.zip" 2>/dev/null; then
            echo "::error::package_web_spa guard passed an incomplete build (AC3 #1100)"
            exit 1
          fi
          # fa1.dev parity pin: both web builds must keep the identical
          # release flags AND the same pinned SDK — the bundle's only edit
          # stays the base tag.
          for wf in .github/workflows/pages.yml .github/workflows/ci.yml; do
            grep -q -- '--release' "$wf" || { echo "::error::$wf lost the --release web flag (#1100 parity)"; exit 1; }
            grep -q -- '--base-href /app/' "$wf" || { echo "::error::$wf lost --base-href /app/ (#1100 parity, pages + bundle must share it)"; exit 1; }
            grep -q "flutter-version: '3.47.x'" "$wf" || { echo "::error::$wf unpinned Flutter SDK (#1100 parity, pages + bundle must share it)"; exit 1; }
          done

      # Issue #433 AC1: README CRAP badge must equal the crap4dart.yaml
      # threshold (they drifted to 8.0-vs-12.0 once). Pure python — runs on
      # every PR, including docs-only ones (a README edit is exactly the
      # drift vector).
      - name: CRAP badge/config sync guard
        run: python3 scripts/check_crap_guards.py

      # gh-1199 AC2: the deterministic-gate boundary is self-enforcing —
      # an integration-tagged test that looks live (real provider URL, or
      # a credential-key literal with no mock/loopback in sight) without
      # the `llm` tag fails the gate. Runs on every PR: a PR adding a live
      # test (E1) is exactly the diff this must catch.

# test (E1) is exactly the diff this must catch.
      - name: LLM tag boundary lint (gh-1199 AC2)
        run: python3 scripts/check_llm_tag_boundary.py

      # gh-1199 AC6/E3: the flake quarantine list itself must stay
      # honest — every entry documented (issue, since, >=2 proving runs)
      # and pointing at an existing integration-tagged file.
      - name: Flake quarantine list guard (gh-1199 AC6)
        run: python3 scripts/apply_quarantine.py --check

      # gh-1296 NG1/AC2: every lockfile in the repo is committed and
      # enforced — ONE inventory list (scripts/check_lockfiles.sh) fails the
      # PR when a listed lockfile is missing, untracked, or gitignored, and
      # the guard's own red exits are fixture-self-tested so the check
      # cannot rot silently (#1100 pattern).
      - name: Lockfile inventory gate (gh-1296 NG1)
        run: bash scripts/check_lockfiles.sh inventory

      - name: Lockfile gate self-test (gh-1296 AC2)
        run: bash scripts/check_lockfiles_selftest.sh

      # gh-1300 AC6: the shard duration-budget gate's own red exits are
      # fixture-self-tested (breach fails + files the body; fit passes;
      # warn band; unbudgeted shard is loud; update is down-only) so the
      # ratchet cannot rot silently (#1100 pattern).
      - name: Duration budget gate self-test (gh-1300 AC6)
        run: bash scripts/duration_budget_selftest.sh

      # Full analyze needs the example app's package config (Flutter imports);
      # a docs-only PR skips the flutter setup entirely and analyzes the pure
      # Dart scopes only — it cannot have changed resolution anyway.
      - uses: subosito/flutter-action@1a449444c387b1966244ae4d4f8c696479add0b2 # v2
        if: needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        with:
          channel: stable
          cache: true

      - name: Example app setup (full analyze only)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          printf 'OPENROUTER_API_KEY=\nMODEL_ID=\nBASE_URL=\nHUGGINGFACE_TOKEN=\n' > [REDACTED:Credential File]
          cp flutter_app/firebase_options.template.dart flutter_app/lib/firebase_options.dart
          dart pub get --directory=office_addin/dart

      - uses: ./.github/actions/flutter-pub-get
        if: needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
      - name: dart analyze (full)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: dart analyze

      - name: dart analyze (docs-only scope)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.app != 'true' && needs.changes.outputs.core != 'true' && needs.changes.outputs.shared != 'true'
        run: dart analyze lib test bin

      # Publish gate at PR time: publish-blocking problems (undeclared lib/
      # imports, stray PEM-like strings) used to surface only in the tag-time
      # publish job — the v0.1.331 era: an undeclared package:cryptography
      # import shipped red on ~26 consecutive tags. --ignore-warnings: the
      # two known layout warnings (gitignored install_local.sh, docs/
      # naming) must not redden every PR, while validation ERRORS — "does
      # not have X in the dependencies section of pubspec.yaml" — still
      # fail. setup-dart (sdk >= 3.13) registers a publish-scoped PUB_TOKEN
      # job-wide and pub.dev rejects authenticated metadata reads, so
      # resolve unauthenticated (same pattern as the publish job);
      # --dry-run never uploads.
      - name: Publish dry-run (unauthenticated)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          dart pub token remove https://pub.dev || true
          # Against the STAGED tree, not the repo root (#597 AC1): the
          # publish job publishes from the stage — the v0.1.407 class of
          # failure (staged resolution re-pinning vendor/dart_tui through
          # pubspec_overrides.yaml) must redden the PR, not the tag.
          bash scripts/stage_publish_package.sh /tmp/pr-dry-run-stage
          # The staged tree must ANALYZE clean: v0.1.411 shipped files
          # with broken imports (the staging filter pruned lib/src/memory;
          # imports of fork-only dart_tui symbols) that only a consumer's
          # `dart analyze` ever surfaced (issue #613). Errors fail the
          # gate; warnings/infos pass, matching the static analyze stage.
          (cd /tmp/pr-dry-run-stage && dart pub get && dart analyze)
          (cd /tmp/pr-dry-run-stage && dart pub publish --dry-run --ignore-warnings)

  test-core:
    # Always runs (no job-level path gate): a path-filtered matrix skip
    # posts a check-run with the LITERAL unrendered name — the required
    # contexts (shard 0..3) never report, and branch protection blocks
    # out-of-scope PRs at 27 green checks. The scope fastpass below
    # green-skips the real steps in seconds instead.
    name: Core tests (shard ${{ matrix.shard }}/4)
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    needs: changes

Senior Code Reviewer & Security Expert You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,

pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. Findings on unchanged code outside the diff belong in `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, not as inline comments. Do NOT write `outputs/response.md`; the review is posted to GitHub only. ```mermaid flowchart TD O1["Write outputs/pr_review.json — structured data for GitHub PR review…
