# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`

## Quality gates (pre-commit hook: `scripts/pre-commit`)

Issue #177 restructured CI so a PR pays only for what it touched. The hook
is a thin wrapper over `scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh`; CI is NOT the same
process — it implements the same stages as parallel jobs, and since
issue #194 its PR path classification runs through the SAME script
(`ci_fast_gate.sh --dry-run` in the `changes` job). One classifier, one
set of thresholds; parity is checkable by diffing the hook's
`GATE_STAGE <name> OK|SKIP` markers against the stages the CI changes job
logs for the same diff. Path filters: docs/markdown/prompts-only →
size+analyze; lib/bin/test/example/pubspec → +tests, coverage, CRAP,
jscpd + cross-module dupx; `test/integration/**` → + `integration-mock`
(issue #551: the no-key legs run per-PR); flutter_app/packages → +dupx,
flutter analyze+tests;
scripts/.github/crap4dart.yaml/unknown → everything (safe default, E2 —
holds in CI too). Hook-only extras: dart format self-heal of staged files
and `scripts/check_goldens.py --quick` (skipped for docs-only commits).

- `dart analyze` + dart format clean (explicit dirs — `yoclip/` is a
  standalone video workspace with its own toolchain); example app also
  `flutter analyze --no-fatal-infos --no-fatal-warnings`.
- `dart test` green (integration-tagged excluded from test-core — issue
  #551: `test/integration/**` changes also run the `integration-mock` leg
  per-PR: no-key legs via `MockLlmServer`, `--exclude-tags llm,browser-ext,
  perf,pty`; child-agent-spawn PTY tests carry `pty` and stay in nightly
  (issue #553). Tag-only CI = llm smoke + publish + binaries; nightly keeps
  the full real-provider suite (pty-integration).
  **The Quality gate is deterministic-only (gh-1199): mock LLM everywhere,
  live models never.** Real-provider files carry
  `@Tags(['integration', 'llm'])` and run ONLY in the tag-only
  provider-smoke job and nightly with secrets — the per-PR integration
  shards exclude them at selection (`shard_files.py --exclude-tag llm`) AND
  at invocation (`--exclude-tags browser-ext,llm`), so a model's mood can
  never block a merge. The boundary is self-enforcing:
  `scripts/check_llm_tag_boundary.py` (static-gate step + pinned audit)
  fails any integration-tagged file that looks live without the `llm` tag;
  `test/scripts/shard_files_llm_boundary_test.dart` proves the shard
  selection stays live-free. Real-model verification belongs to the bench

The repo's quality gates: `dart analyze` + `dart format` clean + `dart test` green. The PR breaks the first and (locally) the third — the pre-commit gate should have caught it; the author's lane had no Dart VM so they skipped. Per review guidelines: red CI = BLOCKING.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`

## Quality gates (pre-commit hook: `scripts/pre-commit`)

Issue #177 restructured CI so a PR pays only for what it touched. The hook
is a thin wrapper over `scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh`; CI is NOT the same
process — it implements the same stages as parallel jobs, and since
issue #194 its PR path classification runs through the SAME script
(`ci_fast_gate.sh --dry-run` in the `changes` job). One classifier, one
set of thresholds; parity is checkable by diffing the hook's
`GATE_STAGE <name> OK|SKIP` markers against the stages the CI changes job
logs for the same diff. Path filters: docs/markdown/prompts-only →
size+analyze; lib/bin/test/example/pubspec → +tests, coverage, CRAP,
jscpd + cross-module dupx; `test/integration/**` → + `integration-mock`
(issue #551: the no-key legs run per-PR); flutter_app/packages → +dupx,
flutter analyze+tests;
scripts/.github/crap4dart.yaml/unknown → everything (safe default, E2 —
holds in CI too). Hook-only extras: dart format self-heal of staged files
and `scripts/check_goldens.py --quick` (skipped for docs-only commits).

- `dart analyze` + dart format clean (explicit dirs — `yoclip/` is a
  standalone video workspace with its own toolchain); example app also
  `flutter analyze --no-fatal-infos --no-fatal-warnings`.
- `dart test` green (integration-tagged excluded from test-core — issue
  #551: `test/integration/**` changes also run the `integration-mock` leg
  per-PR: no-key legs via `MockLlmServer`, `--exclude-tags llm,browser-ext,
  perf,pty`; child-agent-spawn PTY tests carry `pty` and stay in nightly
  (issue #553). Tag-only CI = llm smoke + publish + binaries; nightly keeps
  the full real-provider suite (pty-integration).
  **The Quality gate is deterministic-only (gh-1199): mock LLM everywhere,
  live models never.** Real-provider files carry
  `@Tags(['integration', 'llm'])` and run ONLY in the tag-only
  provider-smoke job and nightly with secrets — the per-PR integration
  shards exclude them at selection (`shard_files.py --exclude-tag llm`) AND
  at invocation (`--exclude-tags browser-ext,llm`), so a model's mood can
  never block a merge. The boundary is self-enforcing:
  `scripts/check_llm_tag_boundary.py` (static-gate step + pinned audit)
  fails any integration-tagged file that looks live without the `llm` tag;
  `test/scripts/shard_files_llm_boundary_test.dart` proves the shard
  selection stays live-free. Real-model verification belongs to the bench

The repo's quality gates: `dart analyze` + `dart format` clean + `dart test` green. The PR breaks the first and (locally) the third — the pre-commit gate should have caught it; the author's lane had no Dart VM so they skipped. Per review guidelines: red CI = BLOCKING.

The rewrite replaces secret values with `[REDACTED:...]` markers — could that change critical-command matching? Critical patterns match things like `rm -rf /`, `git push --force`, etc. Replacing a token literal with `[REDACTED:...]` shouldn't flip a critical match from no to yes... could it flip YES to NO? Only if the critical regex matched the token text itself (unlikely — critical patterns are dangerous commands, not tokens). So the mismatch is benign for approvals. But there's a subtler ordering issue: approval interceptors (bash_interceptor.dart) — let me check what that does; maybe it rewrites commands too (the AC says "the interceptor never rewrites" — H2's mangling filter may be in the model provider, not in fa).

The interceptor is a critical-pattern escalator — unrelated to secret mangling. The H2 "filter" that mangled the filename was external (provider-side filtering), and this PR adds fa's own shape rewriter.

1. **Unconditional, config-blind rewriting.** `redactBashCommandSecretShapes(command)` uses the default `RedactionConfig()`. A host that disabled the vendor layer (RedactionConfig(vendor: disabled) or however it's configured) still gets its commands rewritten, because the tool ignores host config. **Issue A (real): redactor flush ordering vs `_writeChain`.** In the settle path:
```dart
await _writeChain;
if (!_logBroken && _redactor != null) {
  final rest = _redactor.flush();
  if (rest.isNotEmpty) {
    final ops = await _ceiling.ingest(rest);
    ...
```
`await _writeChain` drains writes; then flush appends. But `fanOut` may be called concurrently? No — by settle time, stdout/stderr subs are cancelled. OK. But: `_writeChain` could still be pending when `flush()` runs — no, `await _writeChain` first. Then ops applied directly (not via chain) — after subs cancelled, no more fanOut. Fine.

**Issue B (real, edge): the drain-cap race.** The settle path waits at most 500ms for stream drain, then cancels `_stdoutSub`/`_stderrSub`. If a killed job's chunks are still in flight... cancel() drops pending events. A trailing partial line could be dropped — pre-existing behavior (chunks dropped on kill), redactor doesn't worsen. Fine.

**Issue C (memory): `_carry` unbounded.** A job emitting gigabytes without a newline (e.g. `base64 -w0 bigfile`, `yes | tr -d '\n'`) accumulates in `_carry` indefinitely — memory blowup on the fa process, while the pre-PR code streamed chunks to the ceiling (bounded disk, transient memory). The ceiling bounds the FILE, not the redactor's buffer. With redaction enabled by default for all CLI sessions (`config.redactionPipeline == null ? null : ...` — wired whenever a pipeline exists, which is... let me check when redactionPipeline is non-null; likely always in the CLI). So EVERY background job now buffers its trailing partial line in memory until a newline arrives. `cat 2GB.json` (single-line JSON!) — a minified 2GB JSON file has no newlines → 2GB string in `_carry`. That's a plausible real-world regression (minified bundles, base64). Severity: IMPORTANT. Mitigation: cap the carry (e.g. force-flush at N KB, matching ceiling behavior). Actually wait — even pre-PR, `_ceiling.ingest(chunk)` — the chunk is transient after being written. The `JobLogCeiling` keeps a bounded tail in memory once truncated. So yes, pre-PR memory was bounded; post-PR unbounded per job. IMPORTANT.

**Issue D: redaction BEFORE ceiling interplay.** When the ceiling truncates, the marker etc. fine.

**Issue E: `safe.isNotEmpty` check.** When `_logBroken` is true, `_redactor?.ingest(chunk)` still called — carry keeps buffering, flush skipped (guarded by `!_logBroken`). Memory grows even with broken log — minor.

**Issue F: `fanOut` when `_logBroken` true: `_output.add(chunk)` still happens — good (live stream raw).**

**Issue G: JobLogRedactor buffering vs the "no half-token reaches disk" guarantee.** `ingest` holds back the trailing partial LINE (not just partial token) — so any token on a complete line gets transformed. Transform = RedactionPipeline.redact — operates on the whole multi-line text. Fine.

Yes, IMPORTANT-borderline; I'll put SUGGESTION since no live caller misuses it... Actually the risk is real for future callers: `ShellExecOptions` is a public, copyable options object; passing the same instance to two `start`s is natural (e.g. retries). # AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`

## Quality gates (pre-commit hook: `scripts/pre-commit`)

Issue #177 restructured CI so a PR pays only for what it touched. The hook
is a thin wrapper over `scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh`; CI is NOT the same
process — it implements the same stages as parallel jobs, and since
issue #194 its PR path classification runs through the SAME script
(`ci_fast_gate.sh --dry-run` in the `changes` job). One classifier, one
set of thresholds; parity is checkable by diffing the hook's
`GATE_STAGE <name> OK|SKIP` markers against the stages the CI changes job
logs for the same diff. Path filters: docs/markdown/prompts-only →
size+analyze; lib/bin/test/example/pubspec → +tests, coverage, CRAP,
jscpd + cross-module dupx; `test/integration/**` → + `integration-mock`
(issue #551: the no-key legs run per-PR); flutter_app/packages → +dupx,
flutter analyze+tests;
scripts/.github/crap4dart.yaml/unknown → everything (safe default, E2 —
holds in CI too). Hook-only extras: dart format self-heal of staged files
and `scripts/check_goldens.py --quick` (skipped for docs-only commits).

- `dart analyze` + dart format clean (explicit dirs — `yoclip/` is a
  standalone video workspace with its own toolchain); example app also
  `flutter analyze --no-fatal-infos --no-fatal-warnings`.
- `dart test` green (integration-tagged excluded from test-core — issue
  #551: `test/integration/**` changes also run the `integration-mock` leg
  per-PR: no-key legs via `MockLlmServer`, `--exclude-tags llm,browser-ext,
  perf,pty`; child-agent-spawn PTY tests carry `pty` and stay in nightly
  (issue #553). Tag-only CI = llm smoke + publish + binaries; nightly keeps
  the full real-provider suite (pty-integration).
  **The Quality gate is deterministic-only (gh-1199): mock LLM everywhere,
  live models never.** Real-provider files carry
  `@Tags(['integration', 'llm'])` and run ONLY in the tag-only
  provider-smoke job and nightly with secrets — the per-PR integration
  shards exclude them at selection (`shard_files.py --exclude-tag llm`) AND
  at invocation (`--exclude-tags browser-ext,llm`), so a model's mood can
  never block a merge. The boundary is self-enforcing:
  `scripts/check_llm_tag_boundary.py` (static-gate step + pinned audit)
  fails any integration-tagged file that looks live without the `llm` tag;
  `test/scripts/shard_files_llm_boundary_test.dart` proves the shard

The rewrite replaces secret values with `[REDACTED:...]` markers — could that change critical-command matching? Critical patterns match things like `rm -rf /`, `git push --force`, etc. Replacing a token literal with `[REDACTED:...]` shouldn't flip a critical match from no to yes... could it flip YES to NO? Only if the critical regex matched the token text itself (unlikely — critical patterns are dangerous commands, not tokens). So the mismatch is benign for approvals. But there's a subtler ordering issue: approval interceptors (bash_interceptor.dart) — let me check what that does; maybe it rewrites commands too (the AC says "the interceptor never rewrites" — H2's mangling filter may be in the model provider, not in fa).

The PR claims AC2's redaction pipeline masks tool results and the session record presumably already masks secrets elsewhere (there's a RedactionPipeline used for tool results/session). ```
`await _writeChain` drains writes; then flush appends. But `fanOut` may be called concurrently? No — by settle time, stdout/stderr subs are cancelled. OK. But: `_writeChain` could still be pending when `flush()` runs — no, `await _writeChain` first. Then ops applied directly (not via chain) — after subs cancelled, no more fanOut. Fine.

**Issue B (real, edge): the drain-cap race.** The settle path waits at most 500ms for stream drain, then cancels `_stdoutSub`/`_stderrSub`. If a killed job's chunks are still in flight... cancel() drops pending events. A trailing partial line could be dropped — pre-existing behavior (chunks dropped on kill), redactor doesn't worsen. Fine.

**Issue C (memory): `_carry` unbounded.** A job emitting gigabytes without a newline (e.g. `base64 -w0 bigfile`, `yes | tr -d '\n'`) accumulates in `_carry` indefinitely — memory blowup on the fa process, while the pre-PR code streamed chunks to the ceiling (bounded disk, transient memory). The ceiling bounds the FILE, not the redactor's buffer. With redaction enabled by default for all CLI sessions (`config.redactionPipeline == null ? null : ...` — wired whenever a pipeline exists, which is... let me check when redactionPipeline is non-null; likely always in the CLI). So EVERY background job now buffers its trailing partial line in memory until a newline arrives. `cat 2GB.json` (single-line JSON!) — a minified 2GB JSON file has no newlines → 2GB string in `_carry`. That's a plausible real-world regression (minified bundles, base64). Severity: IMPORTANT. Mitigation: cap the carry (e.g. force-flush at N KB, matching ceiling behavior). Actually wait — even pre-PR, `_ceiling.ingest(chunk)` — the chunk is transient after being written. The `JobLogCeiling` keeps a bounded tail in memory once truncated. - `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`

## Quality gates (pre-commit hook: `scripts/pre-commit`)

Issue #177 restructured CI so a PR pays only for what it touched. The hook
is a thin wrapper over `scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh`; CI is NOT the same
process — it implements the same stages as parallel jobs, and since
issue #194 its PR path classification runs through the SAME script
(`ci_fast_gate.sh --dry-run` in the `changes` job). One classifier, one
set of thresholds; parity is checkable by diffing the hook's
`GATE_STAGE <name> OK|SKIP` markers against the stages the CI changes job
logs for the same diff. Path filters: docs/markdown/prompts-only →
size+analyze; lib/bin/test/example/pubspec → +tests, coverage, CRAP,
jscpd + cross-module dupx; `test/integration/**` → + `integration-mock`
(issue #551: the no-key legs run per-PR); flutter_app/packages → +dupx,
flutter analyze+tests;
scripts/.github/crap4dart.yaml/unknown → everything (safe default, E2 —
holds in CI too). Hook-only extras: dart format self-heal of staged files
and `scripts/check_goldens.py --quick` (skipped for docs-only commits).

- `dart analyze` + dart format clean (explicit dirs — `yoclip/` is a
  standalone video workspace with its own toolchain); example app also
  `flutter analyze --no-fatal-infos --no-fatal-warnings`.
- `dart test` green (integration-tagged excluded from test-core — issue
  #551: `test/integration/**` changes also run the `integration-mock` leg
  per-PR: no-key legs via `MockLlmServer`, `--exclude-tags llm,browser-ext,
  perf,pty`; child-agent-spawn PTY tests carry `pty` and stay in nightly
  (issue #553). Tag-only CI = llm smoke + publish + binaries; nightly keeps
  the full real-provider suite (pty-integration).
  **The Quality gate is deterministic-only (gh-1199): mock LLM everywhere,
  live models never.** Real-provider files carry
  `@Tags(['integration', 'llm'])` and run ONLY in the tag-only
  provider-smoke job and nightly with secrets — the per-PR integration
  shards exclude them at selection (`shard_files.py --exclude-tag llm`) AND
  at invocation (`--exclude-tags browser-ext,llm`), so a model's mood can
  never block a merge. The boundary is self-enforcing:
  `scripts/check_llm_tag_boundary.py` (static-gate step + pinned audit)
  fails any integration-tagged file that looks live without the `llm` tag;
  `test/scripts/shard_files_llm_boundary_test.dart` proves the shard
  selection stays live-free. Real-model verification belongs to the bench

The repo's quality gates: `dart analyze` + `dart format` clean + `dart test` green. The PR breaks the first and (locally) the third — the pre-commit gate should have caught it; the author's lane had no Dart VM so they skipped. Per review guidelines: red CI = BLOCKING.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`

## Quality gates (pre-commit hook: `scripts/pre-commit`)

Issue #177 restructured CI so a PR pays only for what it touched. The hook
is a thin wrapper over `scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh`; CI is NOT the same
process — it implements the same stages as parallel jobs, and since
issue #194 its PR path classification runs through the SAME script
(`ci_fast_gate.sh --dry-run` in the `changes` job). One classifier, one
set of thresholds; parity is checkable by diffing the hook's
`GATE_STAGE <name> OK|SKIP` markers against the stages the CI changes job
logs for the same diff. Path filters: docs/markdown/prompts-only →
size+analyze; lib/bin/test/example/pubspec → +tests, coverage, CRAP,
jscpd + cross-module dupx; `test/integration/**` → + `integration-mock`
(issue #551: the no-key legs run per-PR); flutter_app/packages → +dupx,
flutter analyze+tests;
scripts/.github/crap4dart.yaml/unknown → everything (safe default, E2 —
holds in CI too). Hook-only extras: dart format self-heal of staged files
and `scripts/check_goldens.py --quick` (skipped for docs-only commits).

- `dart analyze` + dart format clean (explicit dirs — `yoclip/` is a
  standalone video workspace with its own toolchain); example app also
  `flutter analyze --no-fatal-infos --no-fatal-warnings`.
- `dart test` green (integration-tagged excluded from test-core — issue
  #551: `test/integration/**` changes also run the `integration-mock` leg
  per-PR: no-key legs via `MockLlmServer`, `--exclude-tags llm,browser-ext,
  perf,pty`; child-agent-spawn PTY tests carry `pty` and stay in nightly
  (issue #553). Tag-only CI = llm smoke + publish + binaries; nightly keeps
  the full real-provider suite (pty-integration).
  **The Quality gate is deterministic-only (gh-1199): mock LLM everywhere,
  live models never.** Real-provider files carry
  `@Tags(['integration', 'llm'])` and run ONLY in the tag-only
  provider-smoke job and nightly with secrets — the per-PR integration
  shards exclude them at selection (`shard_files.py --exclude-tag llm`) AND
  at invocation (`--exclude-tags browser-ext,llm`), so a model's mood can
  never block a merge. The boundary is self-enforcing:
  `scripts/check_llm_tag_boundary.py` (static-gate step + pinned audit)
  fails any integration-tagged file that looks live without the `llm` tag;
  `test/scripts/shard_files_llm_boundary_test.dart` proves the shard
  selection stays live-free. Real-model verification belongs to the bench

The repo's quality gates: `dart analyze` + `dart format` clean + `dart test` green. The PR breaks the first and (locally) the third — the pre-commit gate should have caught it; the author's lane had no Dart VM so they skipped. Per review guidelines: red CI = BLOCKING.

The interceptor is a critical-pattern escalator — unrelated to secret mangling. The H2 "filter" that mangled the filename was external (provider-side filtering), and this PR adds fa's own shape rewriter.

Now the deeper review questions on the shape rewriter at the tool level:

1. **Unconditional, config-blind rewriting.** `redactBashCommandSecretShapes(command)` uses the default `RedactionConfig()`. A host that disabled the vendor layer (RedactionConfig(vendor: disabled) or however it's configured) still gets its commands rewritten, because the tool ignores host config. Inconsistent with `ShellJobRegistry`/CLI which wire the configured pipeline for logs. Also the session transcript records... wait — what does the session record? The tool call arguments as sent (raw command, with the real secret) or the executed one? The agent loop records tool call arguments (raw). The PR claims AC2's redaction pipeline masks tool results and the session record presumably already masks secrets elsewhere (there's a RedactionPipeline used for tool results/session). Not my concern.

2. **Rewrite happens before timeout validation etc.** — fine.

3. **The rewritten command runs but approval UI showed the original** — approval sees arguments (original command). The tool result includes the notice. Acceptable.

4. **`_runForegroundBash` notices**: `final notices = <String>[if (rewriteNotice != null) rewriteNotice];` — previously `notices` collected retry notices? Let me read how `notices` is used later (appended on retries, joined into output). Fine.

5. **Background path**: `'${rewriteNotice == null ? '' : '$rewriteNotice\n'}Started background job ...'` fine.

6. `_awaitJobOutcome` prefixing: notice + handback; notice + rawOutput. Fine.

7. **JWT `\beyJ[A-Za-z0-9_-]+\.[A-Za-z0-9_-]+\.[A-Za-z0-9_-]*\b`** — base64url JWT header always starts `eyJ`. A *filename* like `token_eyJhbGciOi...pem`? Would match and be rewritten — but that's a true shape; contract says shapes get rewritten. OK per design.

Now the JobLogRedactor memory concern. Let me read job_log_ceiling.dart and the full _LocalShellJob to assess the partial-line buffering against the ceiling and check `_applyLogWrite`.

Detailed analysis of `_LocalShellJob` with redactor:

**Issue A (real): redactor flush ordering vs `_writeChain`.** In the settle path:
```dart
await _writeChain;
if (!_logBroken && _redactor != null) {
  final rest = _redactor.flush();
  if (rest.isNotEmpty) {
    final ops = await _ceiling.ingest(rest);
    ...
```
`await _writeChain` drains writes; then flush appends. But `fanOut` may be called concurrently? No — by settle time, stdout/stderr subs are cancelled. OK. But: `_writeChain` could still be pending when `flush()` runs — no, `await _writeChain` first. Then ops applied directly (not via chain) — after subs cancelled, no more fanOut. Fine.

**Issue B (real, edge): the drain-cap race.** The settle path waits at most 500ms for stream drain, then cancels `_stdoutSub`/`_stderrSub`. If a killed job's chunks are still in flight... cancel() drops pending events. A trailing partial line could be dropped — pre-existing behavior (chunks dropped on kill), redactor doesn't worsen. Fine.

**Issue C (memory): `_carry` unbounded.** A job emitting gigabytes without a newline (e.g. `base64 -w0 bigfile`, `yes | tr -d '\n'`) accumulates in `_carry` indefinitely — memory blowup on the fa process, while the pre-PR code streamed chunks to the ceiling (bounded disk, transient memory). The ceiling bounds the FILE, not the redactor's buffer. With redaction enabled by default for all CLI sessions (`config.redactionPipeline == null ? null : ...` — wired whenever a pipeline exists, which is... let me check when redactionPipeline is non-null; likely always in the CLI). So EVERY background job now buffers its trailing partial line in memory until a newline arrives. `cat 2GB.json` (single-line JSON!) — a minified 2GB JSON file has no newlines → 2GB string in `_carry`. That's a plausible real-world regression (minified bundles, base64). Severity: IMPORTANT. Mitigation: cap the carry (e.g. force-flush at N KB, matching ceiling behavior). Actually wait — even pre-PR, `_ceiling.ingest(chunk)` — the chunk is transient after being written. The `JobLogCeiling` keeps a bounded tail in memory once truncated. So yes, pre-PR memory was bounded; post-PR unbounded per job. IMPORTANT.

**Issue D: redaction BEFORE ceiling interplay.** When the ceiling truncates, the marker etc. fine.

**Issue E: `safe.isNotEmpty` check.** When `_logBroken` is true, `_redactor?.ingest(chunk)` still called — carry keeps buffering, flush skipped (guarded by `!_logBroken`). Memory grows even with broken log — minor.

**Issue F: `fanOut` when `_logBroken` true: `_output.add(chunk)` still happens — good (live stream raw).**

**Issue G: JobLogRedactor buffering vs the "no half-token reaches disk" guarantee.** `ingest` holds back the trailing partial LINE (not just partial token) — so any token on a complete line gets transformed. Transform = RedactionPipeline.redact — operates on the whole multi-line text. Fine.

**Issue H: `_awaitJobOutcome` in the bash tool reads `jobs.tail(entry.id)` and `rawOutput` from where?** Let me check `_shellViaJob`: it subscribes to `entry.output` (raw live stream) — so the tool RESULT text contains RAW secrets (unredacted live output) — that's by design ("live output stays raw; at-rest is the contract"). But wait — tool results pass through the redaction pipeline before being stored/shown to the model? The PR says the pipeline "masks tool results" — so the model-facing text is masked at the pipeline level. OK.

**Issue I: `ShellJobRegistry.start` — per-call `options?.jobLogRedactor` is a `JobLogRedactor` (wrapper) while `jobLogRedactor` field is a raw transform. If a caller passes the same options to multiple `start` calls, the same line-buffered wrapper instance is shared across jobs → cross-job buffer pollution (chunks of job B appended to job A's carry; flush at A's settle would write B's partial line into A's log). Current callers: the bash tool creates fresh ShellExecOptions per start and doesn't set jobLogRedactor per-call. Who sets ShellExecOptions.jobLogRedactor per call? Only tests (shell_job_io_test). So latent API hazard, not live bug. SUGGESTION/IMPORTANT-ish. I'd make it a SUGGESTION with clear note, or IMPORTANT? The mixed typing (wrapper in options, function in registry) is a design wart that invites misuse. I'll mark IMPORTANT (API design) — hmm. Guidelines: IMPORTANT = real maintainability issue. Yes, IMPORTANT-borderline; I'll put SUGGESTION since no live caller misuses it... Actually the risk is real for future callers: `ShellExecOptions` is a public, copyable options object; passing the same instance to two `start`s is natural (e.g. retries). The wrapper silently carries state. I'll flag as IMPORTANT with a concrete note. Hmm, but the review verdict: IMPORTANT doesn't block.

Wait, actually let me re-check: in `ShellJobRegistry.start`:
```dart
final redactor = options?.jobLogRedactor ??
    (sessionRedactor == null ? null : JobLogRedactor(sessionRedactor));
```
`options?.jobLogRedactor` — if a caller supplies one AND the registry has a session default, the caller's per-call wins. Per doc "A caller's per-call ShellExecOptions.jobLogRedactor wins over this session default." OK documented.

**Issue J: `LocalShell.startShellJob`/`_LocalShellJob` — when both are null, byte-identical behavior preserved (test asserts). Good.

**Issue K: AC1 — `ShellJobRegistry.start` dir creation.** `jobLogDir ?? '${baseEnv.cwd}/.fah/bash_jobs'`. What about `tail()`/stale-log scanning paths that hardcode `.fah/bash_jobs`? Let me grep shell_jobs.dart for other hardcoded `.fah/bash_jobs` usages (e.g., `_checkStaleOldFormatJobLogs(dir)` uses `dir` — good). What about the `bash_job` tool actions (output tail reads `entry.logPath` — fine). What about the boot sweep (process-table probe scanning the job dir)? # AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`

## Quality gates (pre-commit hook: `scripts/pre-commit`)

Issue #177 restructured CI so a PR pays only for what it touched. The hook
is a thin wrapper over `scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh`; CI is NOT the same
process — it implements the same stages as parallel jobs, and since
issue #194 its PR path classification runs through the SAME script
(`ci_fast_gate.sh --dry-run` in the `changes` job). One classifier, one
set of thresholds; parity is checkable by diffing the hook's
`GATE_STAGE <name> OK|SKIP` markers against the stages the CI changes job
logs for the same diff. Path filters: docs/markdown/prompts-only →
size+analyze; lib/bin/test/example/pubspec → +tests, coverage, CRAP,
jscpd + cross-module dupx; `test/integration/**` → + `integration-mock`
(issue #551: the no-key legs run per-PR); flutter_app/packages → +dupx,
flutter analyze+tests;
scripts/.github/crap4dart.yaml/unknown → everything (safe default, E2 —
holds in CI too). Hook-only extras: dart format self-heal of staged files
and `scripts/check_goldens.py --quick` (skipped for docs-only commits).

- `dart analyze` + dart format clean (explicit dirs — `yoclip/` is a
  standalone video workspace with its own toolchain); example app also
  `flutter analyze --no-fatal-infos --no-fatal-warnings`.
- `dart test` green (integration-tagged excluded from test-core — issue
  #551: `test/integration/**` changes also run the `integration-mock` leg
  per-PR: no-key legs via `MockLlmServer`, `--exclude-tags llm,browser-ext,
  perf,pty`; child-agent-spawn PTY tests carry `pty` and stay in nightly
  (issue #553). Tag-only CI = llm smoke + publish + binaries; nightly keeps
  the full real-provider suite (pty-integration).
  **The Quality gate is deterministic-only (gh-1199): mock LLM everywhere,
  live models never.** Real-provider files carry
  `@Tags(['integration', 'llm'])` and run ONLY in the tag-only
  provider-smoke job and nightly with secrets — the per-PR integration
  shards exclude them at selection (`shard_files.py --exclude-tag llm`) AND
  at invocation (`--exclude-tags browser-ext,llm`), so a model's mood can
  never block a merge. The boundary is self-enforcing:
  `scripts/check_llm_tag_boundary.py` (static-gate step + pinned audit)
  fails any integration-tagged file that looks live without the `llm` tag;
  `test/scripts/shard_files_llm_boundary_test.dart` proves the shard
  selection stays live-free. Real-model verification belongs to the bench

Detailed analysis of `_LocalShellJob` with redactor:

**Issue A (real): redactor flush ordering vs `_writeChain`.** In the settle path:
```dart
await _writeChain;
if (!_logBroken && _redactor != null) {
  final rest = _redactor.flush();
  if (rest.isNotEmpty) {
    final ops = await _ceiling.ingest(rest);
    ...
```
`await _writeChain` drains writes; then flush appends. But `fanOut` may be called concurrently? No — by settle time, stdout/stderr subs are cancelled. OK. But: `_writeChain` could still be pending when `flush()` runs — no, `await _writeChain` first. Then ops applied directly (not via chain) — after subs cancelled, no more fanOut. Fine.

**Issue B (real, edge): the drain-cap race.** The settle path waits at most 500ms for stream drain, then cancels `_stdoutSub`/`_stderrSub`. If a killed job's chunks are still in flight... cancel() drops pending events. A trailing partial line could be dropped — pre-existing behavior (chunks dropped on kill), redactor doesn't worsen. Fine.

**Issue C (memory): `_carry` unbounded.** A job emitting gigabytes without a newline (e.g. `base64 -w0 bigfile`, `yes | tr -d '\n'`) accumulates in `_carry` indefinitely — memory blowup on the fa process, while the pre-PR code streamed chunks to the ceiling (bounded disk, transient memory). The ceiling bounds the FILE, not the redactor's buffer. With redaction enabled by default for all CLI sessions (`config.redactionPipeline == null ? null : ...` — wired whenever a pipeline exists, which is... let me check when redactionPipeline is non-null; likely always in the CLI). So EVERY background job now buffers its trailing partial line in memory until a newline arrives. `cat 2GB.json` (single-line JSON!) — a minified 2GB JSON file has no newlines → 2GB string in `_carry`. That's a plausible real-world regression (minified bundles, base64). Severity: IMPORTANT. Mitigation: cap the carry (e.g. force-flush at N KB, matching ceiling behavior). Actually wait — even pre-PR, `_ceiling.ingest(chunk)` — the chunk is transient after being written. The `JobLogCeiling` keeps a bounded tail in memory once truncated. So yes, pre-PR memory was bounded; post-PR unbounded per job. IMPORTANT.

**Issue D: redaction BEFORE ceiling interplay.** When the ceiling truncates, the marker etc. fine.

**Issue E: `safe.isNotEmpty` check.** When `_logBroken` is true, `_redactor?.ingest(chunk)` still called — carry keeps buffering, flush skipped (guarded by `!_logBroken`). Memory grows even with broken log — minor.

**Issue F: `fanOut` when `_logBroken` true: `_output.add(chunk)` still happens — good (live stream raw).**

**Issue G: JobLogRedactor buffering vs the "no half-token reaches disk" guarantee.** `ingest` holds back the trailing partial LINE (not just partial token) — so any token on a complete line gets transformed. Transform = RedactionPipeline.redact — operates on the whole multi-line text. Fine.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`

## Quality gates (pre-commit hook: `scripts/pre-commit`)

Issue #177 restructured CI so a PR pays only for what it touched. The hook
is a thin wrapper over `scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh`; CI is NOT the same
process — it implements the same stages as parallel jobs, and since
issue #194 its PR path classification runs through the SAME script
(`ci_fast_gate.sh --dry-run` in the `changes` job). One classifier, one
set of thresholds; parity is checkable by diffing the hook's
`GATE_STAGE <name> OK|SKIP` markers against the stages the CI changes job
logs for the same diff. Path filters: docs/markdown/prompts-only →
size+analyze; lib/bin/test/example/pubspec → +tests, coverage, CRAP,
jscpd + cross-module dupx; `test/integration/**` → + `integration-mock`
(issue #551: the no-key legs run per-PR); flutter_app/packages → +dupx,
flutter analyze+tests;
scripts/.github/crap4dart.yaml/unknown → everything (safe default, E2 —
holds in CI too). Hook-only extras: dart format self-heal of staged files
and `scripts/check_goldens.py --quick` (skipped for docs-only commits).

- `dart analyze` + dart format clean (explicit dirs — `yoclip/` is a
  standalone video workspace with its own toolchain); example app also
  `flutter analyze --no-fatal-infos --no-fatal-warnings`.
- `dart test` green (integration-tagged excluded from test-core — issue
  #551: `test/integration/**` changes also run the `integration-mock` leg
  per-PR: no-key legs via `MockLlmServer`, `--exclude-tags llm,browser-ext,
  perf,pty`; child-agent-spawn PTY tests carry `pty` and stay in nightly
  (issue #553). Tag-only CI = llm smoke + publish + binaries; nightly keeps
  the full real-provider suite (pty-integration).
  **The Quality gate is deterministic-only (gh-1199): mock LLM everywhere,
  live models never.** Real-provider files carry
  `@Tags(['integration', 'llm'])` and run ONLY in the tag-only
  provider-smoke job and nightly with secrets — the per-PR integration
  shards exclude them at selection (`shard_files.py --exclude-tag llm`) AND
  at invocation (`--exclude-tags browser-ext,llm`), so a model's mood can
  never block a merge. The boundary is self-enforcing:
  `scripts/check_llm_tag_boundary.py` (static-gate step + pinned audit)
  fails any integration-tagged file that looks live without the `llm` tag;
  `test/scripts/shard_files_llm_boundary_test.dart` proves the shard
  selection stays live-free. Real-model verification belongs to the bench

The repo's quality gates: `dart analyze` + `dart format` clean + `dart test` green. The PR breaks the first and (locally) the third — the pre-commit gate should have caught it; the author's lane had no Dart VM so they skipped. Per review guidelines: red CI = BLOCKING.

Detailed analysis of `_LocalShellJob` with redactor:

**Issue A (real): redactor flush ordering vs `_writeChain`.** In the settle path:
```dart
await _writeChain;
if (!_logBroken && _redactor != null) {
  final rest = _redactor.flush();
  if (rest.isNotEmpty) {
    final ops = await _ceiling.ingest(rest);
    ...
```
`await _writeChain` drains writes; then flush appends. But `fanOut` may be called concurrently? No — by settle time, stdout/stderr subs are cancelled. OK. But: `_writeChain` could still be pending when `flush()` runs — no, `await _writeChain` first. Then ops applied directly (not via chain) — after subs cancelled, no more fanOut. Fine.

**Issue B (real, edge): the drain-cap race.** The settle path waits at most 500ms for stream drain, then cancels `_stdoutSub`/`_stderrSub`. If a killed job's chunks are still in flight... cancel() drops pending events. A trailing partial line could be dropped — pre-existing behavior (chunks dropped on kill), redactor doesn't worsen. Fine.

**Issue C (memory): `_carry` unbounded.** A job emitting gigabytes without a newline (e.g. `base64 -w0 bigfile`, `yes | tr -d '\n'`) accumulates in `_carry` indefinitely — memory blowup on the fa process, while the pre-PR code streamed chunks to the ceiling (bounded disk, transient memory). The ceiling bounds the FILE, not the redactor's buffer. With redaction enabled by default for all CLI sessions (`config.redactionPipeline == null ? null : ...` — wired whenever a pipeline exists, which is... let me check when redactionPipeline is non-null; likely always in the CLI). So EVERY background job now buffers its trailing partial line in memory until a newline arrives. `cat 2GB.json` (single-line JSON!) — a minified 2GB JSON file has no newlines → 2GB string in `_carry`. That's a plausible real-world regression (minified bundles, base64). Severity: IMPORTANT. Mitigation: cap the carry (e.g. force-flush at N KB, matching ceiling behavior). Actually wait — even pre-PR, `_ceiling.ingest(chunk)` — the chunk is transient after being written. The `JobLogCeiling` keeps a bounded tail in memory once truncated. So yes, pre-PR memory was bounded; post-PR unbounded per job. IMPORTANT.

**Issue D: redaction BEFORE ceiling interplay.** When the ceiling truncates, the marker etc. fine.

**Issue E: `safe.isNotEmpty` check.** When `_logBroken` is true, `_redactor?.ingest(chunk)` still called — carry keeps buffering, flush skipped (guarded by `!_logBroken`). Memory grows even with broken log — minor.

**Issue F: `fanOut` when `_logBroken` true: `_output.add(chunk)` still happens — good (live stream raw).**

**Issue G: JobLogRedactor buffering vs the "no half-token reaches disk" guarantee.** `ingest` holds back the trailing partial LINE (not just partial token) — so any token on a complete line gets transformed. Transform = RedactionPipeline.redact — operates on the whole multi-line text. Fine.

**Issue H: `_awaitJobOutcome` in the bash tool reads `jobs.tail(entry.id)` and `rawOutput` from where?** Let me check `_shellViaJob`: it subscribes to `entry.output` (raw live stream) — so the tool RESULT text contains RAW secrets (unredacted live output) — that's by design ("live output stays raw; at-rest is the contract"). But wait — tool results pass through the redaction pipeline before being stored/shown to the model? The PR says the pipeline "masks tool results" — so the model-facing text is masked at the pipeline level. OK.

**Issue I: `ShellJobRegistry.start` — per-call `options?.jobLogRedactor` is a `JobLogRedactor` (wrapper) while `jobLogRedactor` field is a raw transform. If a caller passes the same options to multiple `start` calls, the same line-buffered wrapper instance is shared across jobs → cross-job buffer pollution (chunks of job B appended to job A's carry; flush at A's settle would write B's partial line into A's log). Current callers: the bash tool creates fresh ShellExecOptions per start and doesn't set jobLogRedactor per-call. Who sets ShellExecOptions.jobLogRedactor per call? Only tests (shell_job_io_test). So latent API hazard, not live bug. SUGGESTION/IMPORTANT-ish. I'd make it a SUGGESTION with clear note, or IMPORTANT? The mixed typing (wrapper in options, function in registry) is a design wart that invites misuse. I'll mark IMPORTANT (API design) — hmm. Guidelines: IMPORTANT = real maintainability issue. Yes, IMPORTANT-borderline; I'll put SUGGESTION since no live caller misuses it... Actually the risk is real for future callers: `ShellExecOptions` is a public, copyable options object; passing the same instance to two `start`s is natural (e.g. retries). The wrapper silently carries state. I'll flag as IMPORTANT with a concrete note. Hmm, but the review verdict: IMPORTANT doesn't block.

Wait, actually let me re-check: in `ShellJobRegistry.start`:
```dart
final redactor = options?.jobLogRedactor ??
    (sessionRedactor == null ? null : JobLogRedactor(sessionRedactor));
```
`options?.jobLogRedactor` — if a caller supplies one AND the registry has a session default, the caller's per-call wins. Per doc "A caller's per-call ShellExecOptions.jobLogRedactor wins over this session default." OK documented.

**Issue J: `LocalShell.startShellJob`/`_LocalShellJob` — when both are null, byte-identical behavior preserved (test asserts). Good.

**Issue K: AC1 — `ShellJobRegistry.start` dir creation.** `jobLogDir ?? '${baseEnv.cwd}/.fah/bash_jobs'`. What about `tail()`/stale-log scanning paths that hardcode `.fah/bash_jobs`? Let me grep shell_jobs.dart for other hardcoded `.fah/bash_jobs` usages (e.g., `_checkStaleOldFormatJobLogs(dir)` uses `dir` — good). What about the `bash_job` tool actions (output tail reads `entry.logPath` — fine). What about the boot sweep (process-table probe scanning the job dir)? # AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`

## Quality gates (pre-commit hook: `scripts/pre-commit`)

Issue #177 restructured CI so a PR pays only for what it touched. The hook
is a thin wrapper over `scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh`; CI is NOT the same
process — it implements the same stages as parallel jobs, and since
issue #194 its PR path classification runs through the SAME script
(`ci_fast_gate.sh --dry-run` in the `changes` job). One classifier, one
set of thresholds; parity is checkable by diffing the hook's
`GATE_STAGE <name> OK|SKIP` markers against the stages the CI changes job
logs for the same diff. Path filters: docs/markdown/prompts-only →
size+analyze; lib/bin/test/example/pubspec → +tests, coverage, CRAP,
jscpd + cross-module dupx; `test/integration/**` → + `integration-mock`
(issue #551: the no-key legs run per-PR); flutter_app/packages → +dupx,
flutter analyze+tests;
scripts/.github/crap4dart.yaml/unknown → everything (safe default, E2 —
holds in CI too). Hook-only extras: dart format self-heal of staged files
and `scripts/check_goldens.py --quick` (skipped for docs-only commits).

- `dart analyze` + dart format clean (explicit dirs — `yoclip/` is a
  standalone video workspace with its own toolchain); example app also
  `flutter analyze --no-fatal-infos --no-fatal-warnings`.
- `dart test` green (integration-tagged excluded from test-core — issue
  #551: `test/integration/**` changes also run the `integration-mock` leg
  per-PR: no-key legs via `MockLlmServer`, `--exclude-tags llm,browser-ext,
  perf,pty`; child-agent-spawn PTY tests carry `pty` and stay in nightly
  (issue #553). Tag-only CI = llm smoke + publish + binaries; nightly keeps
  the full real-provider suite (pty-integration).
  **The Quality gate is deterministic-only (gh-1199): mock LLM everywhere,
  live models never.** Real-provider files carry
  `@Tags(['integration', 'llm'])` and run ONLY in the tag-only
  provider-smoke job and nightly with secrets — the per-PR integration
  shards exclude them at selection (`shard_files.py --exclude-tag llm`) AND
  at invocation (`--exclude-tags browser-ext,llm`), so a model's mood can
  never block a merge. The boundary is self-enforcing:
  `scripts/check_llm_tag_boundary.py` (static-gate step + pinned audit)
  fails any integration-tagged file that looks live without the `llm` tag;
  `test/scripts/shard_files_llm_boundary_test.dart` proves the shard
  selection stays live-free. Real-model verification belongs to the bench

The repo's quality gates: `dart analyze` + `dart format` clean + `dart test` green. The PR breaks the first and (locally) the third — the pre-commit gate should have caught it; the author's lane had no Dart VM so they skipped. Per review guidelines: red CI = BLOCKING.

messages.preview: Let me verify the boot path context for `captureLostJobs` and confirm the CLI-level `.fah/bash_jobs` recreation.

blocks.text:
- `agent_hub_cli.dart:381` calls `jobStarted(job)` — the hub CLI records jobs into `<cwd>/.fah/bash_jobs/running.json` regardless of `jobLogDir`.
- `jobSettled` → `_manifestRemove` → `_withRegistryLock` → `createDir('<cwd>/.fah/bash_jobs')`.

So in the CLI path with `FAH_JOB_LOG_DIR` set, every background job (started in hub mode) or every settle (in normal CLI mode) writes/creates `<task-cwd>/.fah/bash_jobs/running.json` and lock dirs. And boot reconcile (`captureLostJobs` → `_reconcileRegistry` → `_withRegistryLock` at line 313) creates `<cwd>/.fah/bash_jobs` at every boot.

This significantly undermines AC1's headline claim: "UT: a run with the override leaves no `.fah/` in the task dir after completion." The UT passes because it builds a bare `ShellJobRegistry` without the CLI waiting layer. In the REAL CLI path, `.fah/bash_jobs` still gets created in the task dir (running.json + lock dir; empty after settle but PRESENT during the run — and the graded diff checks final state; running.json is removed on settle but the `.fah/bash_jobs` DIRECTORY and possibly the lock dir `.fah/bash_jobs/running.json.lock`... `_withRegistryLock` finally removes `_manifestLockPath` (the lock dir). So after a clean run: `.fah/bash_jobs/` directory exists but empty? Let's see: `createDir` creates it; lock dir removed; manifest written at start (`_manifestAdd`) then removed at settle (`_manifestRemove` rewrites the file without the entry — writes `[]` or removes? `_writeRegistry` writes `jsonEncode(entries)` → `[]` stays as a file? `_manifestRemove` rewrites `[]`. So `running.json` containing `[]` REMAINS. Actually wait — `_reconcileRegistry` at boot: "Live entries are KEPT... rewrites the registry when anything changed" — at settle `_manifestRemove` → `_mutateRegistry` → `_writeRegistryEntries(kept)` where kept = entries minus id → `[]` → writes `running.json` = `[]`. So the file remains with `[]`.

Hold on — is this true in the normal (non-hub) CLI? `_onShellJobSettled` → `jobSettled` → manifest remove → creates `.fah/bash_jobs` in the task cwd. Yes — the normal CLI's onSettled hook is registered at agent_cli.dart:418 for the ShellJobRegistry. So EVERY background job in a bench run settles → `jobSettled` → `createDir('<cwd>/.fah/bash_jobs')` + `running.json` = `[]`.

Wait — but does `_mutateRegistry` swallow when nothing changed? Look at `_mutateRegistry`: reads entries under lock, mutates, writes back. For `_manifestRemove`, if the entry isn't there... the mutate function removes by id; if entries was empty, kept == entries; does it write anyway? Line ~380: `await _withRegistryLock(() async { final entries = await _readRegistry(); final kept = mutate(entries); if (quarantined || kept.length != entries.length) { await _writeRegistryEntries(kept); });` — for removal, if kept.length != entries.length → write. On settle the entry WAS added at start (hub mode) → rewrite `[]`. In non-hub mode was anything ever ADDED? `jobStarted` is only called from agent_hub_cli. In plain CLI mode, settle calls `jobSettled` → `_manifestRemove(id)` → kept.length == entries.length (0 == 0) → NO write. BUT `_withRegistryLock` still ran `createDir('<cwd>/.fah/bash_jobs')`! The lock acquisition: `_acquireRegistryLock` — exclusive create of the lock dir `_manifestLockPath` = `<cwd>/.fah/bash_jobs/running.json.lock`. So the plain CLI path STILL creates `<task-cwd>/.fah/bash_jobs/running.json.lock` (then removes the lock dir) — the parent `.fah/bash_jobs` directory remains.

So the AC1 guarantee ("no `.fah/` in the task dir after completion") does NOT hold on the real CLI path — only in the bare-registry UT. The `.fah` directory (empty bash_jobs dir) stays in the graded workspace. Whether `test_no_other_files_changed` counts empty directories: git doesn't track empty dirs, but terminal-bench graded diff may compare directory listings (the original failure was about "extra modified files" — file-level). An empty `.fah/` dir might not flip a git-based diff (git ignores empty dirs), but the harness's own `sanitize-git-repo/.hard` grading may use `find`-style checks. Regardless: the in-repo UT proves the bare registry leaves no `.fah`, but the end-to-end CLI claim is not covered by any test, and the code path contradicts it. This is a genuine IMPORTANT/BLOCKING-ish finding.

Severity call: The AC says "a run with the override leaves no `.fah/` in the task dir after completion" — as implemented (CLI-level), a run still creates `.fah/bash_jobs` via the waiting bookkeeping (and `running.json` in hub mode).
