## Quality gates (pre-commit hook: `scripts/pre-commit`)

Issue #177 restructured CI so a PR pays only for what it touched. The hook
is a thin wrapper over `scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh`; CI is NOT the same
process — it implements the same stages as parallel jobs, and since
issue #194 its PR path classification runs through the SAME script
(`ci_fast_gate.sh --dry-run` in the `changes` job). One classifier, one
set of thresholds; parity is checkable by diffing the hook's
`GATE_STAGE <name> OK|SKIP` markers against the stages the CI changes job
logs for the same diff. Path filters: docs/markdown/prompts-only →
size+analyze; lib/bin/test/example/pubspec → +tests, coverage, CRAP,
jscpd + cross-module dupx; `test/integration/**` → + `integration-mock`
(issue #551: the no-key legs run per-PR); flutter_app/packages → +dupx,
flutter analyze+tests;
scripts/.github/crap4dart.yaml/unknown → everything (safe default, E2 —
holds in CI too). Hook-only extras: dart format self-heal of staged files
and `scripts/check_goldens.py --quick` (skipped for docs-only commits).

- `dart analyze` + dart format clean (explicit dirs — `yoclip/` is a
  standalone video workspace with its own toolchain); example app also
  `flutter analyze --no-fatal-infos --no-fatal-warnings`.
- `dart test` green (integration-tagged excluded from test-core — issue
  #551: `test/integration/**` changes also run the `integration-mock` leg
  per-PR: no-key legs via `MockLlmServer`, `--exclude-tags llm,browser-ext,
  perf,pty`; child-agent-spawn PTY tests carry `pty` and stay in nightly
  (issue #553). Tag-only CI = llm smoke + publish + binaries; nightly keeps
  the full real-provider suite (pty-integration).
  **The Quality gate is deterministic-only (gh-1199): mock LLM everywhere,
  live models never.** Real-provider files carry
  `@Tags(['integration', 'llm'])` and run ONLY in the tag-only
  provider-smoke job and nightly with secrets — the per-PR integration
  shards exclude them at selection (`shard_files.py --exclude-tag llm`) AND
  at invocation (`--exclude-tags browser-ext,llm`), so a model's mood can
  never block a merge. The boundary is self-enforcing:
  `scripts/check_llm_tag_boundary.py` (static-gate step + pinned audit)
  fails any integration-tagged file that looks live without the `llm` tag;
  `test/scripts/shard_files_llm_boundary_test.dart` proves the shard
  selection stays live-free. Real-model verification belongs to the bench

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`

## Quality gates (pre-commit hook: `scripts/pre-commit`)

Issue #177 restructured CI so a PR pays only for what it touched. The hook
is a thin wrapper over `scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh`; CI is NOT the same
process — it implements the same stages as parallel jobs, and since
issue #194 its PR path classification runs through the SAME script
(`ci_fast_gate.sh --dry-run` in the `changes` job). One classifier, one
set of thresholds; parity is checkable by diffing the hook's
`GATE_STAGE <name> OK|SKIP` markers against the stages the CI changes job
logs for the same diff. Path filters: docs/markdown/prompts-only →
size+analyze; lib/bin/test/example/pubspec → +tests, coverage, CRAP,
jscpd + cross-module dupx; `test/integration/**` → + `integration-mock`
(issue #551: the no-key legs run per-PR); flutter_app/packages → +dupx,
flutter analyze+tests;
scripts/.github/crap4dart.yaml/unknown → everything (safe default, E2 —
holds in CI too). Hook-only extras: dart format self-heal of staged files
and `scripts/check_goldens.py --quick` (skipped for docs-only commits).

- `dart analyze` + dart format clean (explicit dirs — `yoclip/` is a
  standalone video workspace with its own toolchain); example app also
  `flutter analyze --no-fatal-infos --no-fatal-warnings`.
- `dart test` green (integration-tagged excluded from test-core — issue
  #551: `test/integration/**` changes also run the `integration-mock` leg
  per-PR: no-key legs via `MockLlmServer`, `--exclude-tags llm,browser-ext,
  perf,pty`; child-agent-spawn PTY tests carry `pty` and stay in nightly
  (issue #553). Tag-only CI = llm smoke + publish + binaries; nightly keeps
  the full real-provider suite (pty-integration).
  **The Quality gate is deterministic-only (gh-1199): mock LLM everywhere,
  live models never.** Real-provider files carry
  `@Tags(['integration', 'llm'])` and run ONLY in the tag-only
  provider-smoke job and nightly with secrets — the per-PR integration
  shards exclude them at selection (`shard_files.py --exclude-tag llm`) AND
  at invocation (`--exclude-tags browser-ext,llm`), so a model's mood can
  never block a merge. The boundary is self-enforcing:
  `scripts/check_llm_tag_boundary.py` (static-gate step + pinned audit)
  fails any integration-tagged file that looks live without the `llm` tag;
  `test/scripts/shard_files_llm_boundary_test.dart` proves the shard
  selection stays live-free. Real-model verification belongs to the bench

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`

## Quality gates (pre-commit hook: `scripts/pre-commit`)

Issue #177 restructured CI so a PR pays only for what it touched. The hook
is a thin wrapper over `scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh`; CI is NOT the same
process — it implements the same stages as parallel jobs, and since
issue #194 its PR path classification runs through the SAME script
(`ci_fast_gate.sh --dry-run` in the `changes` job). One classifier, one
set of thresholds; parity is checkable by diffing the hook's
`GATE_STAGE <name> OK|SKIP` markers against the stages the CI changes job
logs for the same diff. Path filters: docs/markdown/prompts-only →
size+analyze; lib/bin/test/example/pubspec → +tests, coverage, CRAP,
jscpd + cross-module dupx; `test/integration/**` → + `integration-mock`
(issue #551: the no-key legs run per-PR); flutter_app/packages → +dupx,
flutter analyze+tests;
scripts/.github/crap4dart.yaml/unknown → everything (safe default, E2 —
holds in CI too). Hook-only extras: dart format self-heal of staged files
and `scripts/check_goldens.py --quick` (skipped for docs-only commits).

- `dart analyze` + dart format clean (explicit dirs — `yoclip/` is a
  standalone video workspace with its own toolchain); example app also
  `flutter analyze --no-fatal-infos --no-fatal-warnings`.
- `dart test` green (integration-tagged excluded from test-core — issue
  #551: `test/integration/**` changes also run the `integration-mock` leg
  per-PR: no-key legs via `MockLlmServer`, `--exclude-tags llm,browser-ext,
  perf,pty`; child-agent-spawn PTY tests carry `pty` and stay in nightly
  (issue #553). Tag-only CI = llm smoke + publish + binaries; nightly keeps
  the full real-provider suite (pty-integration).
  **The Quality gate is deterministic-only (gh-1199): mock LLM everywhere,
  live models never.** Real-provider files carry
  `@Tags(['integration', 'llm'])` and run ONLY in the tag-only
  provider-smoke job and nightly with secrets — the per-PR integration
  shards exclude them at selection (`shard_files.py --exclude-tag llm`) AND
  at invocation (`--exclude-tags browser-ext,llm`), so a model's mood can
  never block a merge. The boundary is self-enforcing:
  `scripts/check_llm_tag_boundary.py` (static-gate step + pinned audit)
  fails any integration-tagged file that looks live without the `llm` tag;
  `test/scripts/shard_files_llm_boundary_test.dart` proves the shard
  selection stays live-free. Real-model verification belongs to the bench

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`

## Quality gates (pre-commit hook: `scripts/pre-commit`)

Issue #177 restructured CI so a PR pays only for what it touched. The hook
is a thin wrapper over `scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh`; CI is NOT the same
process — it implements the same stages as parallel jobs, and since
issue #194 its PR path classification runs through the SAME script
(`ci_fast_gate.sh --dry-run` in the `changes` job). One classifier, one
set of thresholds; parity is checkable by diffing the hook's
`GATE_STAGE <name> OK|SKIP` markers against the stages the CI changes job
logs for the same diff. Path filters: docs/markdown/prompts-only →
size+analyze; lib/bin/test/example/pubspec → +tests, coverage, CRAP,
jscpd + cross-module dupx; `test/integration/**` → + `integration-mock`
(issue #551: the no-key legs run per-PR); flutter_app/packages → +dupx,
flutter analyze+tests;
scripts/.github/crap4dart.yaml/unknown → everything (safe default, E2 —
holds in CI too). Hook-only extras: dart format self-heal of staged files
and `scripts/check_goldens.py --quick` (skipped for docs-only commits).

- `dart analyze` + dart format clean (explicit dirs — `yoclip/` is a
  standalone video workspace with its own toolchain); example app also
  `flutter analyze --no-fatal-infos --no-fatal-warnings`.
- `dart test` green (integration-tagged excluded from test-core — issue
  #551: `test/integration/**` changes also run the `integration-mock` leg
  per-PR: no-key legs via `MockLlmServer`, `--exclude-tags llm,browser-ext,
  perf,pty`; child-agent-spawn PTY tests carry `pty` and stay in nightly
  (issue #553). Tag-only CI = llm smoke + publish + binaries; nightly keeps
  the full real-provider suite (pty-integration).
  **The Quality gate is deterministic-only (gh-1199): mock LLM everywhere,
  live models never.** Real-provider files carry
  `@Tags(['integration', 'llm'])` and run ONLY in the tag-only
  provider-smoke job and nightly with secrets — the per-PR integration
  shards exclude them at selection (`shard_files.py --exclude-tag llm`) AND
  at invocation (`--exclude-tags browser-ext,llm`), so a model's mood can
  never block a merge. The boundary is self-enforcing:
  `scripts/check_llm_tag_boundary.py` (static-gate step + pinned audit)
  fails any integration-tagged file that looks live without the `llm` tag;
  `test/scripts/shard_files_llm_boundary_test.dart` proves the shard
  selection stays live-free. Real-model verification belongs to the bench

**Another failing test found — in the NEW code, and it fails on this branch right now:**

`test/env/shell_job_io_test.dart:489` — "a secret split across chunks stays redacted (line buffering)":

```dart
final redactor = JobLogRedactor(
  (text) => text.replaceAll('<SECRET>', '[REDACTED]'),   // (unredacted in my view: fixture AWS key)
);
expect(redactor.ingest('key <SEC'), isEmpty);
expect(redactor.ingest('RET>\ndone'), '[REDACTED]\ndone');
```

Wait — the actual output is `'key [REDACTED]\n'` — hmm. My tool output redaction mangled my view of the test. The raw test (per CI-style) is:

```dart
expect(redactor.ingest('key [REDACTED:AWS Access Key]'), isEmpty);
expect(redactor.ingest('[REDACTED:AWS Access Key]\ndone'), '[REDACTED]\ndone');
```

Hmm, no. The failure output shows `Actual: 'key [REDACTED]\n'` — meaning the FIRST ingest returned... wait. Actually the actual value contains "key [REDACTED]\ndone"?? Let me decode carefully. MY OUTPUT redactor is what's mangling: the raw actual is `'key AKIA[REDACTED:AWS Access Key]\ndone'`? No...

Let me think about what the raw test content is. My output pipeline replaces the AWS key literal `[REDACTED:AWS Access Key]` with `[REDACTED:AWS Access Key]`. So:

- Test source line 1: `expect(redactor.ingest('key AKIA'), isEmpty);` — displays as `ingest('key AKIA'), isEmpty`? But in the diff I saw `expect(redactor.ingest('key AKIA'), isEmpty);` — shown already redacted-shortened? In the diff it displayed as `redactor.ingest('key AKIA')` — likely the raw source is `'key [REDACTED:AWS Access Key]'` where the literal AKIA… got replaced INCLUDING the rest. Hmm, that would show `redactor.ingest('key [REDACTED:AWS Access Key]'), isEmpty)` — and the remainder `'IOSFODNN7EXAMPLE\ndone'` shown as the second arg. That matches the diff exactly:
```dart
expect(redactor.ingest('key AKIA'), isEmpty);
expect(redactor.ingest('IOSFODNN7EXAMPLE\ndone'), '[REDACTED]\ndone');
```
So raw source:
```dart
expect(redactor.ingest('key [REDACTED:AWS Access Key]'), isEmpty);
expect(redactor.ingest('\ndone'), '[REDACTED]\ndone');
```
Wait: raw = `'key A' + 'KIAIOSFODNN7EXAMPLE'`? The diff showed two lines: first `'key AKIA'` and second `'IOSFODNN7EXAMPLE\ndone'`. Raw first arg: `'key AKIA'` + `IOSFODNN7EXAMPLE` = `'key [REDACTED:AWS Access Key]'`... but then the marker `[REDACTED:AWS Access Key]` in my display replaced `IOSFODNN7EXAMPLE`?? My redactor replaces `[REDACTED:AWS Access Key]` (the full key). In `key [REDACTED:AWS Access Key]`, the full key IS present (`AKIA` + `IOSFODNN7EXAMPLE`) → displayed as `'key [REDACTED:AWS Access Key]'`. And the second ingest raw arg `'\ndone'`? But display showed `'IOSFODNN7EXAMPLE\ndone'`... that means raw second arg is `IOSFODNN7EXAMPLE\ndone` and the first arg raw is `'key AKIA'`?? Then my display's first arg would show `'key AKIA'` verbatim (no full key → no redaction) — matches. And second arg contains no full key either → shown verbatim `'IOSFODNN7EXAMPLE\ndone'`. And the expected `'[REDACTED]\ndone'` is the transform's replacement (plain string, not the key). OK so the raw test is:

```dart
final redactor = JobLogRedactor(
```

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`

## Quality gates (pre-commit hook: `scripts/pre-commit`)

Issue #177 restructured CI so a PR pays only for what it touched. The hook
is a thin wrapper over `scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh`; CI is NOT the same
process — it implements the same stages as parallel jobs, and since
issue #194 its PR path classification runs through the SAME script
(`ci_fast_gate.sh --dry-run` in the `changes` job). One classifier, one
set of thresholds; parity is checkable by diffing the hook's
`GATE_STAGE <name> OK|SKIP` markers against the stages the CI changes job
logs for the same diff. Path filters: docs/markdown/prompts-only →
size+analyze; lib/bin/test/example/pubspec → +tests, coverage, CRAP,
jscpd + cross-module dupx; `test/integration/**` → + `integration-mock`
(issue #551: the no-key legs run per-PR); flutter_app/packages → +dupx,
flutter analyze+tests;
scripts/.github/crap4dart.yaml/unknown → everything (safe default, E2 —
holds in CI too). Hook-only extras: dart format self-heal of staged files
and `scripts/check_goldens.py --quick` (skipped for docs-only commits).

- `dart analyze` + dart format clean (explicit dirs — `yoclip/` is a
  standalone video workspace with its own toolchain); example app also
  `flutter analyze --no-fatal-infos --no-fatal-warnings`.
- `dart test` green (integration-tagged excluded from test-core — issue
  #551: `test/integration/**` changes also run the `integration-mock` leg
  per-PR: no-key legs via `MockLlmServer`, `--exclude-tags llm,browser-ext,
  perf,pty`; child-agent-spawn PTY tests carry `pty` and stay in nightly
  (issue #553). Tag-only CI = llm smoke + publish + binaries; nightly keeps
  the full real-provider suite (pty-integration).
  **The Quality gate is deterministic-only (gh-1199): mock LLM everywhere,
  live models never.** Real-provider files carry
  `@Tags(['integration', 'llm'])` and run ONLY in the tag-only
  provider-smoke job and nightly with secrets — the per-PR integration
  shards exclude them at selection (`shard_files.py --exclude-tag llm`) AND
  at invocation (`--exclude-tags browser-ext,llm`), so a model's mood can
  never block a merge. The boundary is self-enforcing:
  `scripts/check_llm_tag_boundary.py` (static-gate step + pinned audit)
  fails any integration-tagged file that looks live without the `llm` tag;
  `test/scripts/shard_files_llm_boundary_test.dart` proves the shard
  selection stays live-free. Real-model verification belongs to the bench

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`

## Quality gates (pre-commit hook: `scripts/pre-commit`)

Issue #177 restructured CI so a PR pays only for what it touched. The hook
is a thin wrapper over `scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh`; CI is NOT the same
process — it implements the same stages as parallel jobs, and since
issue #194 its PR path classification runs through the SAME script
(`ci_fast_gate.sh --dry-run` in the `changes` job). One classifier, one
set of thresholds; parity is checkable by diffing the hook's
`GATE_STAGE <name> OK|SKIP` markers against the stages the CI changes job
logs for the same diff. Path filters: docs/markdown/prompts-only →
size+analyze; lib/bin/test/example/pubspec → +tests, coverage, CRAP,
jscpd + cross-module dupx; `test/integration/**` → + `integration-mock`
(issue #551: the no-key legs run per-PR); flutter_app/packages → +dupx,
flutter analyze+tests;
scripts/.github/crap4dart.yaml/unknown → everything (safe default, E2 —
holds in CI too). Hook-only extras: dart format self-heal of staged files
and `scripts/check_goldens.py --quick` (skipped for docs-only commits).

- `dart analyze` + dart format clean (explicit dirs — `yoclip/` is a
  standalone video workspace with its own toolchain); example app also
  `flutter analyze --no-fatal-infos --no-fatal-warnings`.
- `dart test` green (integration-tagged excluded from test-core — issue
  #551: `test/integration/**` changes also run the `integration-mock` leg
  per-PR: no-key legs via `MockLlmServer`, `--exclude-tags llm,browser-ext,
  perf,pty`; child-agent-spawn PTY tests carry `pty` and stay in nightly
  (issue #553). Tag-only CI = llm smoke + publish + binaries; nightly keeps
  the full real-provider suite (pty-integration).
  **The Quality gate is deterministic-only (gh-1199): mock LLM everywhere,
  live models never.** Real-provider files carry
  `@Tags(['integration', 'llm'])` and run ONLY in the tag-only
  provider-smoke job and nightly with secrets — the per-PR integration
  shards exclude them at selection (`shard_files.py --exclude-tag llm`) AND
  at invocation (`--exclude-tags browser-ext,llm`), so a model's mood can
  never block a merge. The boundary is self-enforcing:
  `scripts/check_llm_tag_boundary.py` (static-gate step + pinned audit)
  fails any integration-tagged file that looks live without the `llm` tag;
  `test/scripts/shard_files_llm_boundary_test.dart` proves the shard
  selection stays live-free. Real-model verification belongs to the bench

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`

## Quality gates (pre-commit hook: `scripts/pre-commit`)

Issue #177 restructured CI so a PR pays only for what it touched. The hook
is a thin wrapper over `scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh`; CI is NOT the same
process — it implements the same stages as parallel jobs, and since
issue #194 its PR path classification runs through the SAME script
(`ci_fast_gate.sh --dry-run` in the `changes` job). One classifier, one
set of thresholds; parity is checkable by diffing the hook's
`GATE_STAGE <name> OK|SKIP` markers against the stages the CI changes job
logs for the same diff. Path filters: docs/markdown/prompts-only →
size+analyze; lib/bin/test/example/pubspec → +tests, coverage, CRAP,
jscpd + cross-module dupx; `test/integration/**` → + `integration-mock`
(issue #551: the no-key legs run per-PR); flutter_app/packages → +dupx,
flutter analyze+tests;
scripts/.github/crap4dart.yaml/unknown → everything (safe default, E2 —
holds in CI too). Hook-only extras: dart format self-heal of staged files
and `scripts/check_goldens.py --quick` (skipped for docs-only commits).

- `dart analyze` + dart format clean (explicit dirs — `yoclip/` is a
  standalone video workspace with its own toolchain); example app also
  `flutter analyze --no-fatal-infos --no-fatal-warnings`.
- `dart test` green (integration-tagged excluded from test-core — issue
  #551: `test/integration/**` changes also run the `integration-mock` leg
  per-PR: no-key legs via `MockLlmServer`, `--exclude-tags llm,browser-ext,
  perf,pty`; child-agent-spawn PTY tests carry `pty` and stay in nightly
  (issue #553). Tag-only CI = llm smoke + publish + binaries; nightly keeps
  the full real-provider suite (pty-integration).
  **The Quality gate is deterministic-only (gh-1199): mock LLM everywhere,
  live models never.** Real-provider files carry
  `@Tags(['integration', 'llm'])` and run ONLY in the tag-only
  provider-smoke job and nightly with secrets — the per-PR integration
  shards exclude them at selection (`shard_files.py --exclude-tag llm`) AND
  at invocation (`--exclude-tags browser-ext,llm`), so a model's mood can
  never block a merge. The boundary is self-enforcing:
  `scripts/check_llm_tag_boundary.py` (static-gate step + pinned audit)
  fails any integration-tagged file that looks live without the `llm` tag;
  `test/scripts/shard_files_llm_boundary_test.dart` proves the shard
  selection stays live-free. Real-model verification belongs to the bench

The repo's quality gates: `dart analyze` + `dart format` clean + `dart test` green. The PR breaks the first and (locally) the third — the pre-commit gate should have caught it; the author's lane had no Dart VM so they skipped. Per review guidelines: red CI = BLOCKING.

## Quality gates (pre-commit hook: `scripts/pre-commit`)

Issue #177 restructured CI so a PR pays only for what it touched. The hook
is a thin wrapper over `scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh`; CI is NOT the same
process — it implements the same stages as parallel jobs, and since
issue #194 its PR path classification runs through the SAME script
(`ci_fast_gate.sh --dry-run` in the `changes` job). One classifier, one
set of thresholds; parity is checkable by diffing the hook's
`GATE_STAGE <name> OK|SKIP` markers against the stages the CI changes job
logs for the same diff. Path filters: docs/markdown/prompts-only →
size+analyze; lib/bin/test/example/pubspec → +tests, coverage, CRAP,
jscpd + cross-module dupx; `test/integration/**` → + `integration-mock`
(issue #551: the no-key legs run per-PR); flutter_app/packages → +dupx,
flutter analyze+tests;
scripts/.github/crap4dart.yaml/unknown → everything (safe default, E2 —
holds in CI too). Hook-only extras: dart format self-heal of staged files
and `scripts/check_goldens.py --quick` (skipped for docs-only commits).

- `dart analyze` + dart format clean (explicit dirs — `yoclip/` is a
  standalone video workspace with its own toolchain); example app also
  `flutter analyze --no-fatal-infos --no-fatal-warnings`.
- `dart test` green (integration-tagged excluded from test-core — issue
  #551: `test/integration/**` changes also run the `integration-mock` leg
  per-PR: no-key legs via `MockLlmServer`, `--exclude-tags llm,browser-ext,
  perf,pty`; child-agent-spawn PTY tests carry `pty` and stay in nightly
  (issue #553). Tag-only CI = llm smoke + publish + binaries; nightly keeps
  the full real-provider suite (pty-integration).
  **The Quality gate is deterministic-only (gh-1199): mock LLM everywhere,
  live models never.** Real-provider files carry
  `@Tags(['integration', 'llm'])` and run ONLY in the tag-only
  provider-smoke job and nightly with secrets — the per-PR integration
  shards exclude them at selection (`shard_files.py --exclude-tag llm`) AND
  at invocation (`--exclude-tags browser-ext,llm`), so a model's mood can
  never block a merge. The boundary is self-enforcing:
  `scripts/check_llm_tag_boundary.py` (static-gate step + pinned audit)
  fails any integration-tagged file that looks live without the `llm` tag;
  `test/scripts/shard_files_llm_boundary_test.dart` proves the shard
  selection stays live-free. Real-model verification belongs to the bench

## Quality gates (pre-commit hook: `scripts/pre-commit`)

Issue #177 restructured CI so a PR pays only for what it touched. The hook
is a thin wrapper over `scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh`; CI is NOT the same
process — it implements the same stages as parallel jobs, and since
issue #194 its PR path classification runs through the SAME script
(`ci_fast_gate.sh --dry-run` in the `changes` job). One classifier, one
set of thresholds; parity is checkable by diffing the hook's
`GATE_STAGE <name> OK|SKIP` markers against the stages the CI changes job
logs for the same diff. Path filters: docs/markdown/prompts-only →
size+analyze; lib/bin/test/example/pubspec → +tests, coverage, CRAP,
jscpd + cross-module dupx; `test/integration/**` → + `integration-mock`
(issue #551: the no-key legs run per-PR); flutter_app/packages → +dupx,
flutter analyze+tests;
scripts/.github/crap4dart.yaml/unknown → everything (safe default, E2 —
holds in CI too). Hook-only extras: dart format self-heal of staged files
and `scripts/check_goldens.py --quick` (skipped for docs-only commits).

- `dart analyze` + dart format clean (explicit dirs — `yoclip/` is a
  standalone video workspace with its own toolchain); example app also
  `flutter analyze --no-fatal-infos --no-fatal-warnings`.
- `dart test` green (integration-tagged excluded from test-core — issue
  #551: `test/integration/**` changes also run the `integration-mock` leg
  per-PR: no-key legs via `MockLlmServer`, `--exclude-tags llm,browser-ext,
  perf,pty`; child-agent-spawn PTY tests carry `pty` and stay in nightly
  (issue #553). Tag-only CI = llm smoke + publish + binaries; nightly keeps
  the full real-provider suite (pty-integration).
  **The Quality gate is deterministic-only (gh-1199): mock LLM everywhere,
  live models never.** Real-provider files carry
  `@Tags(['integration', 'llm'])` and run ONLY in the tag-only
  provider-smoke job and nightly with secrets — the per-PR integration
  shards exclude them at selection (`shard_files.py --exclude-tag llm`) AND
  at invocation (`--exclude-tags browser-ext,llm`), so a model's mood can
  never block a merge. The boundary is self-enforcing:
  `scripts/check_llm_tag_boundary.py` (static-gate step + pinned audit)
  fails any integration-tagged file that looks live without the `llm` tag;
  `test/scripts/shard_files_llm_boundary_test.dart` proves the shard
  selection stays live-free. Real-model verification belongs to the bench

The repo's quality gates: `dart analyze` + `dart format` clean + `dart test` green. The PR breaks the first and (locally) the third — the pre-commit gate should have caught it; the author's lane had no Dart VM so they skipped. Per review guidelines: red CI = BLOCKING.

**BLOCKING #2 — a runtime crash in the new core function, on EVERY bash call:**

```
Unsupported operation: Cannot modify an unmodifiable list
dart:_internal  UnmodifiableListMixin.sort
package:flutter_agent_harness/src/approval/bash_shape_redaction.dart 93:7  redactBashCommandSecretShapes
```

`bash_shape_redaction.dart:93`:
```dart
final matches = layerVendor(command, config)
  ..sort((a, b) => a.start.compareTo(b.start));
```

`layerVendor` returns `const []` (a CONST/unmodifiable list) when no matches — the cascade `..sort` on an unmodifiable list throws `UnsupportedError`. Wait — when no matches, `if (matches.isEmpty) return null;` comes AFTER the sort. So for ANY command with no vendor match (the overwhelmingly common case — every plain `ls`, `git status`...), `layerVendor` returns `const []` → `..sort` on unmodifiable → **CRASH**. Every single bash tool call crashes with UnsupportedError!

Wait — but do simple commands hit the empty path? `layerVendor(text, cfg)`: `if (text.isEmpty || !quickScreen(text)) return const [];` — for `ls -la`, quickScreen false → `const []` → sort → CRASH. 🚨 **BLOCKING: `redactBashCommandSecretShapes` crashes the bash tool on (almost) every command**

`layerVendor` returns `const []` when the cheap pre-screen finds no vendor prefix — and the cascade sorts that **unmodifiable** list in place:

```dart
final matches = layerVendor(command, config)
  ..sort((a, b) => a.start.compareTo(b.start));   // ← UnsupportedError on const []
if (matches.isEmpty) return null;
```

Every command without a vendor prefix (`ls -la`, `git status`, `echo hi`, …) throws
`Unsupported operation: Cannot modify an unmodifiable list` at this line — i.e. the
common case, not the edge case. Verified locally:

```
CRASH: Unsupported operation: Cannot modify an unmodifiable list
```

This is what red CI run 37774628085 shows across shards — e.g. 27 failures in
`test/tools/builtin_tools_test.dart`, plus `shell_jobs_test`, PTY/CLI integration
and Flutter-app shards, all with the same stack:

```
dart:_internal                                UnmodifiableListMixin.sort
.../src/approval/bash_shape_redaction.dart 93:7   redactBashCommandSecretShapes
.../src/tools/builtin_tools_bash.dart 170:23      shellTool.<fn>
```

Fix — copy before sorting (and note `layerVendor`'s doc says matches come back
"grouped per pattern"; they are actually interleaved and unsorted across patterns,
hence the sort is needed):

```dart
final matches = [...layerVendor(command, config)]
  ..sort((a, b) => a.start.compareTo(b.start));
if (matches.isEmpty) return null;
```

(The doc comment on `layerVendor` at `lib/src/redact/layer_vendor.dart` — "matches
never overlap (first pattern wins a contested span)" — is what the slicing loop
relies on; that part is correct.)

The AC3 unit tests never caught this because the test file doesn't compile (see the
separate comment on `bash_shape_redaction_test.dart:19`) — please run
`dart analyze lib test bin` and the touched `dart test` files before pushing.

`layerVendor` returns `const []` when the cheap pre-screen finds no vendor prefix — and the cascade sorts that **unmodifiable** list in place:

```dart

  ..sort((a, b) => a.start.compareTo(b.start));   // ← UnsupportedError on const []
if (matches.isEmpty) return null;
```

Every command without a vendor prefix (`ls -la`, `git status`, `echo hi`, …) throws
`Unsupported operation: Cannot modify an unmodifiable list` at this line — i.e. the
common case, not the edge case. Verified locally:

```
CRASH: Unsupported operation: Cannot modify an unmodifiable list
```

This is what red CI run 37774628085 shows across shards — e.g. 27 failures in
`test/tools/builtin_tools_test.dart`, plus `shell_jobs_test`, PTY/CLI integration
and Flutter-app shards, all with the same stack:

```
dart:_internal                                UnmodifiableListMixin.sort
.../src/approval/bash_shape_redaction.dart 93:7   redactBashCommandSecretShapes
.../src/tools/builtin_tools_bash.dart 170:23      shellTool.<fn>
```

Fix — copy before sorting (and note `layerVendor`'s doc says matches come back
"grouped per pattern"; they are actually interleaved and unsorted across patterns,
hence the sort is needed):

```dart
final matches = [...layerVendor(command, config)]
  ..sort((a, b) => a.start.compareTo(b.start));
if (matches.isEmpty) return null;
```

(The doc comment on `layerVendor` at `lib/src/redact/layer_vendor.dart` — "matches
never overlap (first pattern wins a contested span)" — is what the slicing loop
relies on; that part is correct.)

cross-run job registry machinery in `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_waiting.dart` still
hardcodes `<cwd>/.fah/bash_jobs` and is on the boot/settle path of every run:

- `_manifestPath` / `_manifestLockPath` → `<cwd>/.fah/bash_jobs/running.json(.lock)`
  (`agent_cli_waiting.dart:243-256`);
- `_withRegistryLock` **unconditionally** does
  `await _cli._env.createDir('${_cli._env.cwd}/.fah/bash_jobs')`
  (`agent_cli_waiting.dart:461-465`);
- it runs at boot on **both** REPL and headless paths — `captureLostJobs()` at
  `agent_cli.dart:1478` and `:1676`;
- every job settle calls `jobSettled(job)` unconditionally ("the board/waiting
  bookkeeping always runs", `agent_cli_waiting.dart:901`) → same lock path.

So a bench run with `FAH_JOB_LOG_DIR=/tmp/...` exported still creates
`.fah/bash_jobs/` in the graded task workspace at boot, contradicting the AC's
"leaves **no `.fah/`** in the task dir after completion". The new
`shell_jobs_isolation_test.dart` passes only because it constructs a bare
`ShellJobRegistry` and never exercises the CLI wiring.

**into the task dir with the raw command text** — for a non-vendor-shaped secret
on a command line, that is exactly the at-rest leak class AC2 closes for logs.

through the registry manifest/lock/prune paths too — or at minimum
- relocate `_manifestPath` when `jobLogDir` is set,
- add a CLI-level test asserting a full boot + bash background job + settle leaves
  no `.fah/` in a temp task dir with the override set (the registry-level UT does
  not cover the path this AC is actually about).

cross-run job registry machinery in `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_waiting.dart` still
hardcodes `<cwd>/.fah/bash_jobs` and is on the boot/settle path of every run:

- `_manifestPath` / `_manifestLockPath` → `<cwd>/.fah/bash_jobs/running.json(.lock)`
  (`agent_cli_waiting.dart:243-256`);
- `_withRegistryLock` **unconditionally** does

  (`agent_cli_waiting.dart:461-465`);
- it runs at boot on **both** REPL and headless paths — `captureLostJobs()` at
  `agent_cli.dart:1478` and `:1676`;
- every job settle calls `jobSettled(job)` unconditionally ("the board/waiting
  bookkeeping always runs", `agent_cli_waiting.dart:901`) → same lock path.

So a bench run with `FAH_JOB_LOG_DIR=/tmp/...` exported still creates
`.fah/bash_jobs/` in the graded task workspace at boot, contradicting the AC's
"leaves **no `.fah/`** in the task dir after completion". The new

on a command line, that is exactly the at-rest leak class AC2 closes for logs.

through the registry manifest/lock/prune paths too — or at minimum
- relocate `_manifestPath` when `jobLogDir` is set,
- add a CLI-level test asserting a full boot + bash background job + settle leaves

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the command rewrite ignores the host's redaction config — and leaves no path for task-provided token literals**

Two related problems with calling `redactBashCommandSecretShapes(command)` with the
default config:

1. **Config-blind.** The function takes a `RedactionConfig`, but the tool passes
   none, so the default (vendor layer enabled) always applies. A host that sets
   `redact.enabled: false` gets an inconsistent contract: job logs stay raw (the
   pipeline is null → `jobLogRedactor` null in `agent_cli.dart:429`), yet every
   bash command is still rewritten. Same for a config with the vendor layer
   disabled. The `redact:` config section should steer both mechanisms the same
   way — thread the boot-resolved `RedactionConfig` into `shellTool` (new optional
   parameter) and pass it here.

2. **No bash path remains for a legitimate literal.** After this change, any
   command carrying a vendor-shaped token is executed with
   `[REDACTED:<kind>]` substituted — including the two shapes a bench task
   legitimately needs:
   - `export GH_TOKEN=ghp_…` → executes as `export GH_TOKEN=[REDACTED:GitHub Token]`
     (the new test itself pins this rewrite);
   - `echo <token> > ~/.aws/credentials`-style setup → writes the marker into the
     file.

   The notice's advice — "Pass the value as an env var ($NAME) instead of literal
   text" — only works when the value already lives in the process environment.
   When the token arrives as literal text (task description, user chat), there is
   now *no* bash-tool way to materialize it; the agent discovers this only after
   the rewritten command ran. That may be the intended trade-off (secrets never in
   transcripts/logs), but it deterministically fails a whole class of tasks
   (credential-setup benches like the very `configure-git-webserver` autopsy that
   motivated AC3). Please either (a) confirm this is intended and record it in the
   AC3 docs/bench contract, or (b) provide an escape hatch (e.g. skip rewriting
   when the matched literal is registered as a task/user-provided secret via
   `SecretsExecutionEnv`, so approved values still work while unknown ones mask).

`ShellJobRegistry` and never exercises the CLI wiring.

Worse, in hub mode (`agent_hub_cli.dart:381`) `jobStarted()` writes `running.json`
**into the task dir with the raw command text** — for a non-vendor-shaped secret
on a command line, that is exactly the at-rest leak class AC2 closes for logs.

through the registry manifest/lock/prune paths too — or at minimum

{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the command rewrite ignores the host's redaction config — and leaves no path for task-provided token literals**

Two related problems with calling `redactBashCommandSecretShapes(command)` with the
default config:

1. **Config-blind.** The function takes a `RedactionConfig`, but the tool passes
   none, so the default (vendor layer enabled) always applies. A host that sets
   `redact.enabled: false` gets an inconsistent contract: job logs stay raw (the
   pipeline is null → `jobLogRedactor` null in `agent_cli.dart:429`), yet every
   bash command is still rewritten. Same for a config with the vendor layer
   disabled. The `redact:` config section should steer both mechanisms the same
   way — thread the boot-resolved `RedactionConfig` into `shellTool` (new optional
   parameter) and pass it here.

2. **No bash path remains for a legitimate literal.** After this change, any
   command carrying a vendor-shaped token is executed with
   `[REDACTED:<kind>]` substituted — including the two shapes a bench task
   legitimately needs:
   - `export GH_TOKEN=ghp_…` → executes as `export GH_TOKEN=[REDACTED:GitHub Token]`
     (the new test itself pins this rewrite);
   - `echo <token> > ~/.aws/credentials`-style setup → writes the marker into the
     file.

   The notice's advice — "Pass the value as an env var ($NAME) instead of literal
   text" — only works when the value already lives in the process environment.
   When the token arrives as literal text (task description, user chat), there is
   now *no* bash-tool way to materialize it; the agent discovers this only after
   the rewritten command ran. That may be the intended trade-off (secrets never in
   transcripts/logs), but it deterministically fails a whole class of tasks
   (credential-setup benches like the very `configure-git-webserver` autopsy that
   motivated AC3). Please either (a) confirm this is intended and record it in the
   AC3 docs/bench contract, or (b) provide an escape hatch (e.g. skip rewriting
   when the matched literal is registered as a task/user-provided secret via
   `SecretsExecutionEnv`, so approved values still work while unknown ones mask).

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: `_carry` buffers a newline-free output stream without bound — regresses the #919 "bounded job logs" invariant for memory**

`JobLogRedactor.ingest` holds back everything after the last `\n`:

```dart
_carry = buffered.substring(cut + 1);
```

A job that emits no newline (`cat minified-2GB.json`, `base64 -w0 bigfile`,
`yes | tr -d '\n'`) accumulates its **entire output** in `_carry` on the fa heap.
Before this change every chunk flowed straight into `JobLogCeiling.ingest` — the
ceiling bounds the *file* and the in-memory tail (`_maxTailBytes`), and chunk
strings stayed transient; now memory grows at the job's output rate with no cap,
and the ceiling never sees a byte until the first newline. Issue #919's lesson
(the 335 GB log that OOM'd the host) applies to the redactor buffer too.

Suggest a cap in `ingest`, e.g. force-flush the oldest carry once it exceeds a
bound (a few MB), or cap-and-drop with a one-line `[… redaction buffer overflow …]`
marker — the at-rest redaction guarantee only truly needs to hold for
newline-terminated lines and the final partial line, so document whatever bound
you pick:

```dart
static const _maxCarryBytes = 1 << 20; // 1 MiB partial-line budget
```

Also note `fanOut` still calls `_redactor?.ingest(chunk)` after `_logBroken` —
harmless but wasteful; skipping ingest when the log is broken avoids growing the
carry for a job whose log can no longer be written.

{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the command rewrite ignores the host's redaction config — and leaves no path for task-provided token literals**

Two related problems with calling `redactBashCommandSecretShapes(command)` with the
default config:

1. **Config-blind.** The function takes a `RedactionConfig`, but the tool passes
   none, so the default (vendor layer enabled) always applies. A host that sets
   `redact.enabled: false` gets an inconsistent contract: job logs stay raw (the
   pipeline is null → `jobLogRedactor` null in `agent_cli.dart:429`), yet every
   bash command is still rewritten. Same for a config with the vendor layer
   disabled. The `redact:` config section should steer both mechanisms the same
   way — thread the boot-resolved `RedactionConfig` into `shellTool` (new optional
   parameter) and pass it here.

2. **No bash path remains for a legitimate literal.** After this change, any
   command carrying a vendor-shaped token is executed with
   `[REDACTED:<kind>]` substituted — including the two shapes a bench task
   legitimately needs:
   - `export GH_TOKEN=ghp_…` → executes as `export GH_TOKEN=[REDACTED:GitHub Token]`
     (the new test itself pins this rewrite);
   - `echo <token> > ~/.aws/credentials`-style setup → writes the marker into the
     file.

   The notice's advice — "Pass the value as an env var ($NAME) instead of literal
   text" — only works when the value already lives in the process environment.
   When the token arrives as literal text (task description, user chat), there is
   now *no* bash-tool way to materialize it; the agent discovers this only after
   the rewritten command ran. That may be the intended trade-off (secrets never in
   transcripts/logs), but it deterministically fails a whole class of tasks
   (credential-setup benches like the very `configure-git-webserver` autopsy that
   motivated AC3). Please either (a) confirm this is intended and record it in the
   AC3 docs/bench contract, or (b) provide an escape hatch (e.g. skip rewriting
   when the matched literal is registered as a task/user-provided secret via
   `SecretsExecutionEnv`, so approved values still work while unknown ones mask).

{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: `_carry` buffers a newline-free output stream without bound — regresses the #919 "bounded job logs" invariant for memory**

`JobLogRedactor.ingest` holds back everything after the last `\n`:

```dart
_carry = buffered.substring(cut + 1);
```

A job that emits no newline (`cat minified-2GB.json`, `base64 -w0 bigfile`,
`yes | tr -d '\n'`) accumulates its **entire output** in `_carry` on the fa heap.
Before this change every chunk flowed straight into `JobLogCeiling.ingest` — the
ceiling bounds the *file* and the in-memory tail (`_maxTailBytes`), and chunk
strings stayed transient; now memory grows at the job's output rate with no cap,
and the ceiling never sees a byte until the first newline. Issue #919's lesson
(the 335 GB log that OOM'd the host) applies to the redactor buffer too.

Suggest a cap in `ingest`, e.g. force-flush the oldest carry once it exceeds a
bound (a few MB), or cap-and-drop with a one-line `[… redaction buffer overflow …]`
marker — the at-rest redaction guarantee only truly needs to hold for
newline-terminated lines and the final partial line, so document whatever bound
you pick:

```dart
static const _maxCarryBytes = 1 << 20; // 1 MiB partial-line budget
```

Also note `fanOut` still calls `_redactor?.ingest(chunk)` after `_logBroken` —
harmless but wasteful; skipping ingest when the log is broken avoids growing the
carry for a job whose log can no longer be written.

{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the command rewrite ignores the host's redaction config — and leaves no path for task-provided token literals**

Two related problems with calling `redactBashCommandSecretShapes(command)` with the
default config:

1. **Config-blind.** The function takes a `RedactionConfig`, but the tool passes
   none, so the default (vendor layer enabled) always applies. A host that sets
   `redact.enabled: false` gets an inconsistent contract: job logs stay raw (the
   pipeline is null → `jobLogRedactor` null in `agent_cli.dart:429`), yet every
   bash command is still rewritten. Same for a config with the vendor layer
   disabled. The `redact:` config section should steer both mechanisms the same
   way — thread the boot-resolved `RedactionConfig` into `shellTool` (new optional
   parameter) and pass it here.

2. **No bash path remains for a legitimate literal.** After this change, any
   command carrying a vendor-shaped token is executed with
   `[REDACTED:<kind>]` substituted — including the two shapes a bench task
   legitimately needs:
   - `export GH_TOKEN=ghp_…` → executes as `export GH_TOKEN=[REDACTED:GitHub Token]`
     (the new test itself pins this rewrite);
   - `echo <token> > ~/.aws/credentials`-style setup → writes the marker into the

{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: `_carry` buffers a newline-free output stream without bound — regresses the #919 "bounded job logs" invariant for memory**

`JobLogRedactor.ingest` holds back everything after the last `\n`:

```dart
_carry = buffered.substring(cut + 1);
```

A job that emits no newline (`cat minified-2GB.json`, `base64 -w0 bigfile`,
`yes | tr -d '\n'`) accumulates its **entire output** in `_carry` on the fa heap.
Before this change every chunk flowed straight into `JobLogCeiling.ingest` — the
ceiling bounds the *file* and the in-memory tail (`_maxTailBytes`), and chunk
strings stayed transient; now memory grows at the job's output rate with no cap,
and the ceiling never sees a byte until the first newline. Issue #919's lesson
(the 335 GB log that OOM'd the host) applies to the redactor buffer too.

Suggest a cap in `ingest`, e.g. force-flush the oldest carry once it exceeds a
bound (a few MB), or cap-and-drop with a one-line `[… redaction buffer overflow …]`
marker — the at-rest redaction guarantee only truly needs to hold for
newline-terminated lines and the final partial line, so document whatever bound
you pick:

```dart
static const _maxCarryBytes = 1 << 20; // 1 MiB partial-line budget
```

Also note `fanOut` still calls `_redactor?.ingest(chunk)` after `_logBroken` —
harmless but wasteful; skipping ingest when the log is broken avoids growing the
carry for a job whose log can no longer be written.

{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the command rewrite ignores the host's redaction config — and leaves no path for task-provided token literals**

Two related problems with calling `redactBashCommandSecretShapes(command)` with the
default config:

1. **Config-blind.** The function takes a `RedactionConfig`, but the tool passes
   none, so the default (vendor layer enabled) always applies. A host that sets
   `redact.enabled: false` gets an inconsistent contract: job logs stay raw (the
   pipeline is null → `jobLogRedactor` null in `agent_cli.dart:429`), yet every
   bash command is still rewritten. Same for a config with the vendor layer
   disabled. The `redact:` config section should steer both mechanisms the same
   way — thread the boot-resolved `RedactionConfig` into `shellTool` (new optional
   parameter) and pass it here.

2. **No bash path remains for a legitimate literal.** After this change, any
   command carrying a vendor-shaped token is executed with
   `[REDACTED:<kind>]` substituted — including the two shapes a bench task
   legitimately needs:
   - `export GH_TOKEN=ghp_…` → executes as `export GH_TOKEN=[REDACTED:GitHub Token]`
     (the new test itself pins this rewrite);
   - `echo <token> > ~/.aws/credentials`-style setup → writes the marker into the
     file.

   The notice's advice — "Pass the value as an env var ($NAME) instead of literal
   text" — only works when the value already lives in the process environment.
   When the token arrives as literal text (task description, user chat), there is
   now *no* bash-tool way to materialize it; the agent discovers this only after
   the rewritten command ran. That may be the intended trade-off (secrets never in
   transcripts/logs), but it deterministically fails a whole class of tasks
   (credential-setup benches like the very `configure-git-webserver` autopsy that
   motivated AC3). Please either (a) confirm this is intended and record it in the
   AC3 docs/bench contract, or (b) provide an escape hatch (e.g. skip rewriting
   when the matched literal is registered as a task/user-provided secret via
   `SecretsExecutionEnv`, so approved values still work while unknown ones mask).

{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: `_carry` buffers a newline-free output stream without bound — regresses the #919 "bounded job logs" invariant for memory**

`JobLogRedactor.ingest` holds back everything after the last `\n`:

```dart
_carry = buffered.substring(cut + 1);
```

A job that emits no newline (`cat minified-2GB.json`, `base64 -w0 bigfile`,
`yes | tr -d '\n'`) accumulates its **entire output** in `_carry` on the fa heap.
Before this change every chunk flowed straight into `JobLogCeiling.ingest` — the
ceiling bounds the *file* and the in-memory tail (`_maxTailBytes`), and chunk
strings stayed transient; now memory grows at the job's output rate with no cap,
and the ceiling never sees a byte until the first newline. Issue #919's lesson
(the 335 GB log that OOM'd the host) applies to the redactor buffer too.

Suggest a cap in `ingest`, e.g. force-flush the oldest carry once it exceeds a
bound (a few MB), or cap-and-drop with a one-line `[… redaction buffer overflow …]`
marker — the at-rest redaction guarantee only truly needs to hold for
newline-terminated lines and the final partial line, so document whatever bound
you pick:

```dart
static const _maxCarryBytes = 1 << 20; // 1 MiB partial-line budget
```

{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the command rewrite ignores the host's redaction config — and leaves no path for task-provided token literals**

Two related problems with calling `redactBashCommandSecretShapes(command)` with the
default config:

1. **Config-blind.** The function takes a `RedactionConfig`, but the tool passes
   none, so the default (vendor layer enabled) always applies. A host that sets
   `redact.enabled: false` gets an inconsistent contract: job logs stay raw (the
   pipeline is null → `jobLogRedactor` null in `agent_cli.dart:429`), yet every
   bash command is still rewritten. Same for a config with the vendor layer
   disabled. The `redact:` config section should steer both mechanisms the same
   way — thread the boot-resolved `RedactionConfig` into `shellTool` (new optional
   parameter) and pass it here.

2. **No bash path remains for a legitimate literal.** After this change, any
   command carrying a vendor-shaped token is executed with
   `[REDACTED:<kind>]` substituted — including the two shapes a bench task
   legitimately needs:
   - `export GH_TOKEN=ghp_…` → executes as `export GH_TOKEN=[REDACTED:GitHub Token]`
     (the new test itself pins this rewrite);
   - `echo <token> > ~/.aws/credentials`-style setup → writes the marker into the
     file.

   The notice's advice — "Pass the value as an env var ($NAME) instead of literal
   text" — only works when the value already lives in the process environment.
   When the token arrives as literal text (task description, user chat), there is
   now *no* bash-tool way to materialize it; the agent discovers this only after
   the rewritten command ran. That may be the intended trade-off (secrets never in
   transcripts/logs), but it deterministically fails a whole class of tasks
   (credential-setup benches like the very `configure-git-webserver` autopsy that
   motivated AC3). Please either (a) confirm this is intended and record it in the
   AC3 docs/bench contract, or (b) provide an escape hatch (e.g. skip rewriting
   when the matched literal is registered as a task/user-provided secret via
   `SecretsExecutionEnv`, so approved values still work while unknown ones mask).

{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: `_carry` buffers a newline-free output stream without bound — regresses the #919 "bounded job logs" invariant for memory**

`JobLogRedactor.ingest` holds back everything after the last `\n`:

```dart
_carry = buffered.substring(cut + 1);
```

A job that emits no newline (`cat minified-2GB.json`, `base64 -w0 bigfile`,
`yes | tr -d '\n'`) accumulates its **entire output** in `_carry` on the fa heap.
Before this change every chunk flowed straight into `JobLogCeiling.ingest` — the
ceiling bounds the *file* and the in-memory tail (`_maxTailBytes`), and chunk
strings stayed transient; now memory grows at the job's output rate with no cap,
and the ceiling never sees a byte until the first newline. Issue #919's lesson
(the 335 GB log that OOM'd the host) applies to the redactor buffer too.

Suggest a cap in `ingest`, e.g. force-flush the oldest carry once it exceeds a
bound (a few MB), or cap-and-drop with a one-line `[… redaction buffer overflow …]`
marker — the at-rest redaction guarantee only truly needs to hold for
newline-terminated lines and the final partial line, so document whatever bound
you pick:

```dart
static const _maxCarryBytes = 1 << 20; // 1 MiB partial-line budget
```

Also note `fanOut` still calls `_redactor?.ingest(chunk)` after `_logBroken` —
harmless but wasteful; skipping ingest when the log is broken avoids growing the
carry for a job whose log can no longer be written.

**Summary**: The bash tool is broken by this PR — `redactBashCommandSecretShapes` throws `UnsupportedError` on every command without a vendor-shaped token (`..sort` on the `const []` `layerVendor` returns), which is what reddened CI run 37774628085 across the core/PTY/app shards (27 `builtin_tools_test` failures, PTY/CLI integration, Flutter app). The new Dart tests were never compiled (2 analyzer errors in `bash_shape_redaction_test.dart`) and one AC2 test fails as written; additionally, the AC1 "no `.fah/` in the task dir" guarantee only holds for the bare `ShellJobRegistry` — the CLI's cross-run job bookkeeping (`agent_cli_waiting.dart`) still recreates `.fah/bash_jobs` in the graded workspace at boot and on every settle (and hub-mode `running.json` stores raw command text).

**Key Issues**:
- 🚨 BLOCKING: bash tool crash on the common path (`bash_shape_redaction.dart:92-93`)
- 🚨 BLOCKING: red Static gate — test file doesn't compile (lines 19, 30/36) + failing line-buffering test (`shell_job_io_test.dart:489-490`)
- 🚨 BLOCKING: AC1 end-to-end gap — `.fah/bash_jobs` recreated in the task dir by CLI bookkeeping despite `FAH_JOB_LOG_DIR`
- ⚠️ IMPORTANT: command rewrite ignores the host `redact:` config; no bash path remains for task-provided token literals
- ⚠️ IMPORTANT: `JobLogRedactor._carry` buffers newline-free output unboundedly (regresses the #919 bounded-memory invariant)

**Next Steps**:
1. Copy before sort in `redactBashCommandSecretShapes`; run `dart analyze lib test bin` and the three touched Dart test files before pushing (the two compile errors + wrong flush expectation are all caught by that in seconds)
2. Thread the job-artifacts dir through `agent_cli_waiting.dart`'s manifest/lock/prune paths and add a CLI-level isolation test (boot + background job + settle ⇒ no `.fah/` in the task dir)
3. Decide and document the config story for AC3 (thread `RedactionConfig` / escape hatch for registered secrets) and cap the redactor's carry buffer

Non-blocking notes: flutter_app's `AgentService` registry (line 762) doesn't wire `jobLogRedactor` though the app has `_redactionPipeline` (AC2 parity); 4 diff files are not `dart format`-clean (`bin/fah_runapp.dart`, `lib/src/tools/shell_jobs.dart`, both new test files) — the pre-commit self-heal will rewrite them on next touch. AC4's no-code root-cause documentation is consistent with the traced env path.

`layerVendor` returns `const []` when the cheap pre-screen finds no vendor prefix — and the cascade sorts that **unmodifiable** list in place:

Every command without a vendor prefix (`ls -la`, `git status`, `echo hi`, …) throws

`test/tools/builtin_tools_test.dart`, plus `shell_jobs_test`, PTY/CLI integration
and Flutter-app shards, all with the same stack:

```
.../src/approval/bash_shape_redaction.dart 93:7   redactBashCommandSecretShapes
```
