Fix — copy before sorting (and note `layerVendor`'s doc says matches come back

never overlap (first pattern wins a contested span)" — is what the slicing loop

{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the command rewrite ignores the host's redaction config — and leaves no path for task-provided token literals**

Two related problems with calling `redactBashCommandSecretShapes(command)` with the
default config:

1. **Config-blind.** The function takes a `RedactionConfig`, but the tool passes
   none, so the default (vendor layer enabled) always applies. A host that sets
   `redact.enabled: false` gets an inconsistent contract: job logs stay raw (the
   pipeline is null → `jobLogRedactor` null in `agent_cli.dart:429`), yet every
   bash command is still rewritten. Same for a config with the vendor layer
   disabled. The `redact:` config section should steer both mechanisms the same
   way — thread the boot-resolved `RedactionConfig` into `shellTool` (new optional
   parameter) and pass it here.

2. **No bash path remains for a legitimate literal.** After this change, any
   command carrying a vendor-shaped token is executed with
   `[REDACTED:<kind>]` substituted — including the two shapes a bench task
   legitimately needs:
   - `export GH_TOKEN=ghp_…` → executes as `export GH_TOKEN=[REDACTED:GitHub Token]`
     (the new test itself pins this rewrite);
   - `echo <token> > ~/.aws/credentials`-style setup → writes the marker into the
     file.

   The notice's advice — "Pass the value as an env var ($NAME) instead of literal
   text" — only works when the value already lives in the process environment.
   When the token arrives as literal text (task description, user chat), there is
   now *no* bash-tool way to materialize it; the agent discovers this only after
   the rewritten command ran. That may be the intended trade-off (secrets never in
   transcripts/logs), but it deterministically fails a whole class of tasks
   (credential-setup benches like the very `configure-git-webserver` autopsy that
   motivated AC3). Please either (a) confirm this is intended and record it in the
   AC3 docs/bench contract, or (b) provide an escape hatch (e.g. skip rewriting
   when the matched literal is registered as a task/user-provided secret via
   `SecretsExecutionEnv`, so approved values still work while unknown ones mask).

{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: `_carry` buffers a newline-free output stream without bound — regresses the #919 "bounded job logs" invariant for memory**

`JobLogRedactor.ingest` holds back everything after the last `\n`:

```dart
_carry = buffered.substring(cut + 1);
```

A job that emits no newline (`cat minified-2GB.json`, `base64 -w0 bigfile`,
`yes | tr -d '\n'`) accumulates its **entire output** in `_carry` on the fa heap.
Before this change every chunk flowed straight into `JobLogCeiling.ingest` — the
ceiling bounds the *file* and the in-memory tail (`_maxTailBytes`), and chunk
strings stayed transient; now memory grows at the job's output rate with no cap,
and the ceiling never sees a byte until the first newline. Issue #919's lesson
(the 335 GB log that OOM'd the host) applies to the redactor buffer too.

Suggest a cap in `ingest`, e.g. force-flush the oldest carry once it exceeds a
bound (a few MB), or cap-and-drop with a one-line `[… redaction buffer overflow …]`
marker — the at-rest redaction guarantee only truly needs to hold for
newline-terminated lines and the final partial line, so document whatever bound
you pick:

```dart
static const _maxCarryBytes = 1 << 20; // 1 MiB partial-line budget
```

Also note `fanOut` still calls `_redactor?.ingest(chunk)` after `_logBroken` —
harmless but wasteful; skipping ingest when the log is broken avoids growing the
carry for a job whose log can no longer be written.

{"path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment1.md","content":"🚨 **BLOCKING: `redactBashCommandSecretShapes` crashes the bash tool on (almost) every command**

`layerVendor` returns `const []` when the cheap pre-screen finds no vendor prefix — and the cascade sorts that **unmodifiable** list in place:

```dart
final matches = layerVendor(command, config)
  ..sort((a, b) => a.start.compareTo(b.start));   // ← UnsupportedError on const []
if (matches.isEmpty) return null;
```

Every command without a vendor prefix (`ls -la`, `git status`, `echo hi`, …) throws
`Unsupported operation: Cannot modify an unmodifiable list` at this line — i.e. the
common case, not the edge case. Verified locally:

```
CRASH: Unsupported operation: Cannot modify an unmodifiable list
```

This is what red CI run 37774628085 shows across shards — e.g. 27 failures in
`test/tools/builtin_tools_test.dart`, plus `shell_jobs_test`, PTY/CLI integration
and Flutter-app shards, all with the same stack:

```
dart:_internal                                UnmodifiableListMixin.sort
.../src/approval/bash_shape_redaction.dart 93:7   redactBashCommandSecretShapes
.../src/tools/builtin_tools_bash.dart 170:23      shellTool.<fn>
```

Fix — copy before sorting (and note `layerVendor`'s doc says matches come back
"grouped per pattern"; they are actually interleaved and unsorted across patterns,
hence the sort is needed):

```dart
final matches = [...layerVendor(command, config)]
  ..sort((a, b) => a.start.compareTo(b.start));
if (matches.isEmpty) return null;
```

(The doc comment on `layerVendor` at `lib/src/redact/layer_vendor.dart` — "matches
never overlap (first pattern wins a contested span)" — is what the slicing loop
relies on; that part is correct.)

The AC3 unit tests never caught this because the test file doesn't compile (see the
separate comment on `bash_shape_redaction_test.dart:19`) — please run
`dart analyze lib test bin` and the touched `dart test` files before pushing.

{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the command rewrite ignores the host's redaction config — and leaves no path for task-provided token literals**

Two related problems with calling `redactBashCommandSecretShapes(command)` with the
default config:

1. **Config-blind.** The function takes a `RedactionConfig`, but the tool passes
   none, so the default (vendor layer enabled) always applies. A host that sets
   `redact.enabled: false` gets an inconsistent contract: job logs stay raw (the
   pipeline is null → `jobLogRedactor` null in `agent_cli.dart:429`), yet every
   bash command is still rewritten. Same for a config with the vendor layer
   disabled. The `redact:` config section should steer both mechanisms the same
   way — thread the boot-resolved `RedactionConfig` into `shellTool` (new optional
   parameter) and pass it here.

2. **No bash path remains for a legitimate literal.** After this change, any
   command carrying a vendor-shaped token is executed with
   `[REDACTED:<kind>]` substituted — including the two shapes a bench task
   legitimately needs:
   - `export GH_TOKEN=ghp_…` → executes as `export GH_TOKEN=[REDACTED:GitHub Token]`
     (the new test itself pins this rewrite);
   - `echo <token> > ~/.aws/credentials`-style setup → writes the marker into the
     file.

   The notice's advice — "Pass the value as an env var ($NAME) instead of literal
   text" — only works when the value already lives in the process environment.
   When the token arrives as literal text (task description, user chat), there is
   now *no* bash-tool way to materialize it; the agent discovers this only after
   the rewritten command ran. That may be the intended trade-off (secrets never in
   transcripts/logs), but it deterministically fails a whole class of tasks
   (credential-setup benches like the very `configure-git-webserver` autopsy that
   motivated AC3). Please either (a) confirm this is intended and record it in the
   AC3 docs/bench contract, or (b) provide an escape hatch (e.g. skip rewriting
   when the matched literal is registered as a task/user-provided secret via
   `SecretsExecutionEnv`, so approved values still work while unknown ones mask).

{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: `_carry` buffers a newline-free output stream without bound — regresses the #919 "bounded job logs" invariant for memory**

`JobLogRedactor.ingest` holds back everything after the last `\n`:

```dart
_carry = buffered.substring(cut + 1);
```

A job that emits no newline (`cat minified-2GB.json`, `base64 -w0 bigfile`,
`yes | tr -d '\n'`) accumulates its **entire output** in `_carry` on the fa heap.
Before this change every chunk flowed straight into `JobLogCeiling.ingest` — the
ceiling bounds the *file* and the in-memory tail (`_maxTailBytes`), and chunk
strings stayed transient; now memory grows at the job's output rate with no cap,
and the ceiling never sees a byte until the first newline. Issue #919's lesson
(the 335 GB log that OOM'd the host) applies to the redactor buffer too.

Suggest a cap in `ingest`, e.g. force-flush the oldest carry once it exceeds a
bound (a few MB), or cap-and-drop with a one-line `[… redaction buffer overflow …]`
marker — the at-rest redaction guarantee only truly needs to hold for
newline-terminated lines and the final partial line, so document whatever bound
you pick:

```dart
static const _maxCarryBytes = 1 << 20; // 1 MiB partial-line budget
```

Also note `fanOut` still calls `_redactor?.ingest(chunk)` after `_logBroken` —
harmless but wasteful; skipping ingest when the log is broken avoids growing the
carry for a job whose log can no longer be written.
","path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment5.md"}

{"content":"🚨 **BLOCKING (AC1 gap): the "no `.fah/` in the task dir" guarantee only holds for the bare registry — the CLI bookkeeping still recreates `.fah/bash_jobs` in the workspace**

Wiring `jobLogDir: config.jobLogDir` here relocates the **log files**, but the
cross-run job registry machinery in `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_waiting.dart` still
hardcodes `<cwd>/.fah/bash_jobs` and is on the boot/settle path of every run:

- `_manifestPath` / `_manifestLockPath` → `<cwd>/.fah/bash_jobs/running.json(.lock)`
  (`agent_cli_waiting.dart:243-256`);
- `_withRegistryLock` **unconditionally** does
  `await _cli._env.createDir('${_cli._env.cwd}/.fah/bash_jobs')`
  (`agent_cli_waiting.dart:461-465`);
- it runs at boot on **both** REPL and headless paths — `captureLostJobs()` at
  `agent_cli.dart:1478` and `:1676`;
- every job settle calls `jobSettled(job)` unconditionally ("the board/waiting
  bookkeeping always runs", `agent_cli_waiting.dart:901`) → same lock path.

So a bench run with `FAH_JOB_LOG_DIR=/tmp/...` exported still creates
`.fah/bash_jobs/` in the graded task workspace at boot, contradicting the AC's
"leaves **no `.fah/`** in the task dir after completion". The new
`shell_jobs_isolation_test.dart` passes only because it constructs a bare
`ShellJobRegistry` and never exercises the CLI wiring.

Worse, in hub mode (`agent_hub_cli.dart:381`) `jobStarted()` writes `running.json`
**into the task dir with the raw command text** — for a non-vendor-shaped secret
on a command line, that is exactly the at-rest leak class AC2 closes for logs.

Suggested rework: thread `config.jobLogDir` (a session-scoped "job artifacts dir")
through the registry manifest/lock/prune paths too — or at minimum
- relocate `_manifestPath` when `jobLogDir` is set,
- add a CLI-level test asserting a full boot + bash background job + settle leaves
  no `.fah/` in a temp task dir with the override set (the registry-level UT does
  not cover the path this AC is actually about).

{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the command rewrite ignores the host's redaction config — and leaves no path for task-provided token literals**

Two related problems with calling `redactBashCommandSecretShapes(command)` with the
default config:

1. **Config-blind.** The function takes a `RedactionConfig`, but the tool passes
   none, so the default (vendor layer enabled) always applies. A host that sets
   `redact.enabled: false` gets an inconsistent contract: job logs stay raw (the
   pipeline is null → `jobLogRedactor` null in `agent_cli.dart:429`), yet every
   bash command is still rewritten. Same for a config with the vendor layer
   disabled. The `redact:` config section should steer both mechanisms the same
   way — thread the boot-resolved `RedactionConfig` into `shellTool` (new optional
   parameter) and pass it here.

2. **No bash path remains for a legitimate literal.** After this change, any
   command carrying a vendor-shaped token is executed with
   `[REDACTED:<kind>]` substituted — including the two shapes a bench task
   legitimately needs:
   - `export GH_TOKEN=ghp_…` → executes as `export GH_TOKEN=[REDACTED:GitHub Token]`
     (the new test itself pins this rewrite);
   - `echo <token> > ~/.aws/credentials`-style setup → writes the marker into the
     file.

   The notice's advice — "Pass the value as an env var ($NAME) instead of literal
   text" — only works when the value already lives in the process environment.
   When the token arrives as literal text (task description, user chat), there is
   now *no* bash-tool way to materialize it; the agent discovers this only after
   the rewritten command ran. That may be the intended trade-off (secrets never in
   transcripts/logs), but it deterministically fails a whole class of tasks
   (credential-setup benches like the very `configure-git-webserver` autopsy that
   motivated AC3). Please either (a) confirm this is intended and record it in the
   AC3 docs/bench contract, or (b) provide an escape hatch (e.g. skip rewriting
   when the matched literal is registered as a task/user-provided secret via
   `SecretsExecutionEnv`, so approved values still work while unknown ones mask).

{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: `_carry` buffers a newline-free output stream without bound — regresses the #919 "bounded job logs" invariant for memory**

`JobLogRedactor.ingest` holds back everything after the last `\n`:

```dart
_carry = buffered.substring(cut + 1);
```

A job that emits no newline (`cat minified-2GB.json`, `base64 -w0 bigfile`,
`yes | tr -d '\n'`) accumulates its **entire output** in `_carry` on the fa heap.
Before this change every chunk flowed straight into `JobLogCeiling.ingest` — the
ceiling bounds the *file* and the in-memory tail (`_maxTailBytes`), and chunk
strings stayed transient; now memory grows at the job's output rate with no cap,
and the ceiling never sees a byte until the first newline. Issue #919's lesson
(the 335 GB log that OOM'd the host) applies to the redactor buffer too.

Suggest a cap in `ingest`, e.g. force-flush the oldest carry once it exceeds a
bound (a few MB), or cap-and-drop with a one-line `[… redaction buffer overflow …]`
marker — the at-rest redaction guarantee only truly needs to hold for
newline-terminated lines and the final partial line, so document whatever bound
you pick:

```dart
static const _maxCarryBytes = 1 << 20; // 1 MiB partial-line budget
```

Also note `fanOut` still calls `_redactor?.ingest(chunk)` after `_logBroken` —
harmless but wasteful; skipping ingest when the log is broken avoids growing the
carry for a job whose log can no longer be written.
","path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment5.md"}

```dart
final matches = layerVendor(command, config)
  ..sort((a, b) => a.start.compareTo(b.start));
if (matches.isEmpty) return null;
```
Fix: `final matches = [...layerVendor(command, config)]..sort(...)` or sort a copy, and check empty before sorting.

{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the command rewrite ignores the host's redaction config — and leaves no path for task-provided token literals**

Two related problems with calling `redactBashCommandSecretShapes(command)` with the
default config:

1. **Config-blind.** The function takes a `RedactionConfig`, but the tool passes
   none, so the default (vendor layer enabled) always applies. A host that sets
   `redact.enabled: false` gets an inconsistent contract: job logs stay raw (the
   pipeline is null → `jobLogRedactor` null in `agent_cli.dart:429`), yet every
   bash command is still rewritten. Same for a config with the vendor layer
   disabled. The `redact:` config section should steer both mechanisms the same
   way — thread the boot-resolved `RedactionConfig` into `shellTool` (new optional
   parameter) and pass it here.

2. **No bash path remains for a legitimate literal.** After this change, any
   command carrying a vendor-shaped token is executed with
   `[REDACTED:<kind>]` substituted — including the two shapes a bench task
   legitimately needs:
   - `export GH_TOKEN=ghp_…` → executes as `export GH_TOKEN=[REDACTED:GitHub Token]`
     (the new test itself pins this rewrite);
   - `echo <token> > ~/.aws/credentials`-style setup → writes the marker into the
     file.

   The notice's advice — "Pass the value as an env var ($NAME) instead of literal
   text" — only works when the value already lives in the process environment.
   When the token arrives as literal text (task description, user chat), there is
   now *no* bash-tool way to materialize it; the agent discovers this only after
   the rewritten command ran. That may be the intended trade-off (secrets never in
   transcripts/logs), but it deterministically fails a whole class of tasks
   (credential-setup benches like the very `configure-git-webserver` autopsy that
   motivated AC3). Please either (a) confirm this is intended and record it in the
   AC3 docs/bench contract, or (b) provide an escape hatch (e.g. skip rewriting
   when the matched literal is registered as a task/user-provided secret via
   `SecretsExecutionEnv`, so approved values still work while unknown ones mask).

A job that emits no newline (`cat minified-2GB.json`, `base64 -w0 bigfile`,
`yes | tr -d '\n'`) accumulates its **entire output** in `_carry` on the fa heap.
Before this change every chunk flowed straight into `JobLogCeiling.ingest` — the
ceiling bounds the *file* and the in-memory tail (`_maxTailBytes`), and chunk
strings stayed transient; now memory grows at the job's output rate with no cap,
and the ceiling never sees a byte until the first newline. Issue #919's lesson
(the 335 GB log that OOM'd the host) applies to the redactor buffer too.

Suggest a cap in `ingest`, e.g. force-flush the oldest carry once it exceeds a
bound (a few MB), or cap-and-drop with a one-line `[… redaction buffer overflow …]`
marker — the at-rest redaction guarantee only truly needs to hold for
newline-terminated lines and the final partial line, so document whatever bound
you pick:

```dart
static const _maxCarryBytes = 1 << 20; // 1 MiB partial-line budget
```

Also note `fanOut` still calls `_redactor?.ingest(chunk)` after `_logBroken` —
harmless but wasteful; skipping ingest when the log is broken avoids growing the
carry for a job whose log can no longer be written.

🚨 **BLOCKING 1 — bash tool crashes on the common path.** `redactBashCommandSecretShapes` (bash_shape_redaction.dart:92-93) cascades `..sort` onto the `const []` that `layerVendor` returns for any command without a vendor prefix → `UnsupportedError` on essentially every bash call. Reproduced locally; this is what reddened CI run 37774628085 (27 `builtin_tools_test` failures + shell_jobs/PTY/CLI/Flutter-app shards share the same stack). Fix: `[...layerVendor(...)]..sort(...)`.

🚨 **BLOCKING 2 — red Static gate; tests never compiled.** `test/approval/bash_shape_redaction_test.dart` has 2 analyzer errors (`_textOf` declared `ToolExecutionResult` but returns `String`; `const Ok(...)` infers `Ok<...,dynamic>` vs `Result<...,ExecutionError>`), and `test/env/shell_job_io_test.dart:489-490` fails as written (split-chunk expectations contradict the line-buffer contract: `ingest` returns `'key [REDACTED]\n'`, `flush()` returns `'done'`). 🚨 **BLOCKING 3 — AC1 gap.** The "no `.fah/` in the task dir" guarantee holds only for the bare `ShellJobRegistry`: `agent_cli_waiting.dart` still hardcodes `<cwd>/.fah/bash_jobs` (`_withRegistryLock` unconditionally `createDir`s it; runs at boot via `captureLostJobs` on both REPL/headless paths and on every job settle), and hub-mode `jobStarted` writes `running.json` with raw command text into the task dir — the leak class AC1/AC2 target.

⚠️ IMPORTANT: the command rewrite ignores the host `redact:` config (default `RedactionConfig` hardcoded at the call site — even `redact.enabled: false` hosts get commands rewritten), and no bash path remains for task-provided token literals (`export GH_TOKEN=ghp_…` executes with the marker; the notice's "use an env var" advice doesn't cover literals). ⚠️ IMPORTANT: `JobLogRedactor._carry` buffers newline-free output unboundedly, regressing the #919 bounded-memory invariant.

💡 SUGGESTIONs: rewrite notice prepended before tail-truncation gets dropped on long outputs; `[REDACTED:<label>]` marker literal duplicated from `redaction_pipeline.dart:198`; harbor adapter hardcodes the job-log path instead of a shared constant. General comment also notes: flutter_app `AgentService` registry doesn't wire `jobLogRedactor` (AC2 parity), and 4 diff files aren't `dart format`-clean.

All 7 inline anchors verified as added lines on the RIGHT side of the diff; `issueCounts.blocking=3` is consistent with the 🚨 markers. AC4's documented no-code root cause checks out against the traced env path.

.../src/approval/bash_shape_redaction.dart 93:7   redactBashCommandSecretShapes

cross-run job registry machinery in `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_waiting.dart` still
hardcodes `<cwd>/.fah/bash_jobs` and is on the boot/settle path of every run:

- `_manifestPath` / `_manifestLockPath` → `<cwd>/.fah/bash_jobs/running.json(.lock)`
  (`agent_cli_waiting.dart:243-256`);
- `_withRegistryLock` **unconditionally** does
  `await _cli._env.createDir('${_cli._env.cwd}/.fah/bash_jobs')`
  (`agent_cli_waiting.dart:461-465`);
- it runs at boot on **both** REPL and headless paths — `captureLostJobs()` at
  `agent_cli.dart:1478` and `:1676`;
- every job settle calls `jobSettled(job)` unconditionally ("the board/waiting
  bookkeeping always runs", `agent_cli_waiting.dart:901`) → same lock path.

So a bench run with `FAH_JOB_LOG_DIR=/tmp/...` exported still creates
`.fah/bash_jobs/` in the graded task workspace at boot, contradicting the AC's
"leaves **no `.fah/`** in the task dir after completion". The new
`shell_jobs_isolation_test.dart` passes only because it constructs a bare
`ShellJobRegistry` and never exercises the CLI wiring.

Worse, in hub mode (`agent_hub_cli.dart:381`) `jobStarted()` writes `running.json`
**into the task dir with the raw command text** — for a non-vendor-shaped secret
on a command line, that is exactly the at-rest leak class AC2 closes for logs.

through the registry manifest/lock/prune paths too — or at minimum
- relocate `_manifestPath` when `jobLogDir` is set,

{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the command rewrite ignores the host's redaction config — and leaves no path for task-provided token literals**

Two related problems with calling `redactBashCommandSecretShapes(command)` with the
default config:

1. **Config-blind.** The function takes a `RedactionConfig`, but the tool passes
   none, so the default (vendor layer enabled) always applies. A host that sets
   `redact.enabled: false` gets an inconsistent contract: job logs stay raw (the
   pipeline is null → `jobLogRedactor` null in `agent_cli.dart:429`), yet every
   bash command is still rewritten. Same for a config with the vendor layer
   disabled. The `redact:` config section should steer both mechanisms the same
   way — thread the boot-resolved `RedactionConfig` into `shellTool` (new optional
   parameter) and pass it here.

2. **No bash path remains for a legitimate literal.** After this change, any
   command carrying a vendor-shaped token is executed with
   `[REDACTED:<kind>]` substituted — including the two shapes a bench task
   legitimately needs:
   - `export GH_TOKEN=ghp_…` → executes as `export GH_TOKEN=[REDACTED:GitHub Token]`
     (the new test itself pins this rewrite);
   - `echo <token> > ~/.aws/credentials`-style setup → writes the marker into the
     file.

   The notice's advice — "Pass the value as an env var ($NAME) instead of literal
   text" — only works when the value already lives in the process environment.
   When the token arrives as literal text (task description, user chat), there is
   now *no* bash-tool way to materialize it; the agent discovers this only after
   the rewritten command ran. That may be the intended trade-off (secrets never in
   transcripts/logs), but it deterministically fails a whole class of tasks
   (credential-setup benches like the very `configure-git-webserver` autopsy that
   motivated AC3). Please either (a) confirm this is intended and record it in the
   AC3 docs/bench contract, or (b) provide an escape hatch (e.g. skip rewriting
   when the matched literal is registered as a task/user-provided secret via
   `SecretsExecutionEnv`, so approved values still work while unknown ones mask).

{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: `_carry` buffers a newline-free output stream without bound — regresses the #919 "bounded job logs" invariant for memory**

`JobLogRedactor.ingest` holds back everything after the last `\n`:

```dart
_carry = buffered.substring(cut + 1);
```

A job that emits no newline (`cat minified-2GB.json`, `base64 -w0 bigfile`,
`yes | tr -d '\n'`) accumulates its **entire output** in `_carry` on the fa heap.
Before this change every chunk flowed straight into `JobLogCeiling.ingest` — the
ceiling bounds the *file* and the in-memory tail (`_maxTailBytes`), and chunk
strings stayed transient; now memory grows at the job's output rate with no cap,
and the ceiling never sees a byte until the first newline. Issue #919's lesson
(the 335 GB log that OOM'd the host) applies to the redactor buffer too.

Suggest a cap in `ingest`, e.g. force-flush the oldest carry once it exceeds a
bound (a few MB), or cap-and-drop with a one-line `[… redaction buffer overflow …]`
marker — the at-rest redaction guarantee only truly needs to hold for
newline-terminated lines and the final partial line, so document whatever bound
you pick:

```dart
static const _maxCarryBytes = 1 << 20; // 1 MiB partial-line budget
```

Also note `fanOut` still calls `_redactor?.ingest(chunk)` after `_logBroken` —
harmless but wasteful; skipping ingest when the log is broken avoids growing the
carry for a job whose log can no longer be written.
